docs.title: GregTech Nexus Addon
docs.text:
An addon for GregTech CEu Modern on Minecraft 1.20.1: a steam age that is a real factory tier, wireless steam and EU, AE2 automation, and 170 multiblocks from the steam age to the end of the game.

Install Browse the multiblocks

docs.title: Steam age
docs.text:
Large steam machines with parallel, primitive machines that need no energy, hydraulic parts and a Steam Elevator.

Steam age

docs.title: No pipes, no cables
docs.text:
One steam pool and one EU balance per player, reachable from anywhere.

Wireless steam · Nexus energy

docs.title: AE2 automation
docs.text:
Pattern Buffers that hold patterns, circuits, catalysts and machine modes for any multiblock.

ME Pattern Buffers

docs.title: 170 multiblocks
docs.text:
Ports from GT: Not Leisure, GregTech Odyssey, GregTech Leisure, GT: New Horizons and Twist Space Technology, plus GTNA originals. Every one has a page.

Catalog

docs.title: Endgame
docs.text:
Forge of the Gods, Eye of Harmony, Bose-Einstein Condensate, Space Elevator, Nano Forge and Dyson Sphere, with every formula.

Systems

docs.title: For modpacks
docs.text:
KubeJS bindings, auxiliary modules for any multiblock, balance files and a research engine.

KubeJS API

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Installation: what to install, and in which versions.
  • First steps: when each part of GTNA shows up.
  • Configuration: every option and balance file.
  • FAQ and changelog.

GTNA is free software (LGPLv3), with ported assets under their own licences; see the credits. Questions and reports: GitHub issues or Discord. This wiki is available in English, Português and 简体中文; help translate it.

docs.title: New multiblocks: the naquadah reactor ladder
docs.text:
• Large Naquadah Reactor (from GregTech Odyssey): burns Naquadah Fuel or Enriched Naquadah Fuel with hydrogen at 2,097,152 EU/t (UHV), or with oxygen or nitrogen plasma at 524,288 EU/t for 32 times as long. Up to 3 fluid input hatches; dynamo or laser source hatch.
  • Naquadah Hyper Reactor (GTNA original, 96 × 38 × 24): the best naquadah reactor. Same fuels at UEV, four times the EU per mB. Oxygen plasma gives 8x parallel, nitrogen plasma 16x (40 mB per boosted run). Hatches go in the ring around the controller.
  • New fluids Naquadah Fuel and Enriched Naquadah Fuel, with default Large Chemical Reactor recipes at UV; modpacks can replace them by id.
  • New block Extreme Strength Tritanium Casing (GregTech Odyssey texture).

docs.title: Kinetic Orbital Lance screen
docs.text:
• The target is drawn as itself (craters, Psyche's metal glint, Europa's cracks, Arrokoth's two lobes, Nexus-1's lattice) and orbits on the display; the slug crosses the firing arc after a shot and the impact flashes; returning capsules travel back along the arc.
  • The orbital map moves: bodies orbit at Kepler-like speeds, the Sun pulses, a marching line points at the target, the selected body has a turning ring, and clicks pick the body where it is drawn. Labels no longer overlap or run under the card. The card shows the body, the bodies to survey first when it is locked, and the correct capsule time (it showed the old linear formula).
  • The display shows time to a full bank, the time to the next capsule landing, and says when Nexus-1 needs Magnetarium ingots. Over-budget mass or heat turns red on the bench, and lit rails pulse.
  • The field manual no longer says heavier slugs carry more or that the bank grows with rings.

docs.title: Original multiblocks: progression fixes
docs.text:
• Dimensional Rift Gate: every recorded harmonic raises the maximum depth by 5 (base 5). With the five surface harmonics a consonant chord reaches the Civilisation Relic (depth 20) and the tritone the Void (depth 40), so Precursor Residue and Void Ash can be obtained; the depth was stuck at 8 before.
  • Antimatter Collider Ring: the e+e- proposal no longer locks the ring into electron beams that quenched every second. It unlocks an e+e- button: electron beams stop at 100 GeV per beam (like LEP), count twice in physics runs, and protons come back with one click. Heavy ions, the neutronium magnet and X-Nexus are reachable again.
  • Kinetic Orbital Lance: the aim asks for up to 2^20 CWU/t instead of 16,000, so a Supercomputing Center network keeps improving the accuracy on far bodies.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• mods.toml now declares Applied Energistics 2 as required: GTNA never loaded without it, and Forge now says so instead of crashing. The unused Stargate Journey entry is gone.
  • The Thread Hatch tooltip no longer says it only works in the Duration Tester and KubeJS machines; it names machines that use it.
  • The Forge of the Gods TCT upgrade text now describes the formula the code uses (SA ×3 in the Melting Core and in the Power Forge with DoP, ×2 elsewhere).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• The wiki is rebuilt in English, Portuguese and Simplified Chinese, checked against the code; the language switcher no longer leaves the site (#4). A Translating page explains how to add a language.
  • Formulas on the wiki are typeset with LaTeX (MathJax).
  • New wiki pages, in the three languages: one per original multiblock (Kinetic Orbital Lance, Dimensional Rift Gate, Antimatter Collider Ring, Stellar Containment Chamber) with formulas, tables computed from the code, current screens and known issues; the naquadah reactors; the planned Pressurized Water Reactor. The old Portuguese-only design sheets are no longer published.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: • GTNA needs GTCEu 7.5.3 or newer; with an older GTCEu, Forge now stops with a missing-dependency message. The crash in #1 (NoSuchFieldError: CLUSTER_MAX_HARVESTABLES with GTNA 0.1.0 and GTCEu 7.4.1) came from that old pairing; update both mods.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: • GTNA now requires GTIA Lib 0.5.0 or newer. The multiblock module registry moved there (com.gtinfinityascension.gtialib.module.ModuleRegistry); GTNASubPatterns keeps working and forwards to it. Int128, BlockPosLongSet and BlockPosHashing moved there (com.gtinfinityascension.gtialib.data); addons that imported them from GTNA must update the import.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• 10 recipes failed to load because they used item forms that do not exist: Space Drone MK II, MK V and MK VI asked for quadruple wires of Duranium, Americium and Darmstadtium (no cable in GTCEu); they now use Europium (UHV cable) and the UXV superconductor. Ytterbium, Thallium, Erbium, Hafnium, Rhenium and Gadolinium get a dust form, so the ore processing, stellar synthesis and rare earth recipes that output them load.
  • 0.6.0 failed to load on clients without JEI (EMI-only packs): a debug command named a JEI type in a class every client loads. The JEI part is now its own class, registered only with JEI installed, and a unit test fails if a JEI type appears outside JEI-only classes.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Multiblock preview shapes are cached with a soft reference: EMI builds the shapes of every multiblock when it reloads, and keeping them all made clients with little memory run out of it; the JVM now drops them under memory pressure and rebuilds them on demand.
  • Single-block machines no longer build a list of their covers several times per tick to look for the infinity covers. With 2,000 working LV Electric Furnaces a server tick drops from 8.37 ms to 3.74 ms (−55 %): the six sides are read once per machine per tick for both infinity covers.

docs.title: Original multiblocks: endgame role
docs.text:
• Each original now produces something only it makes, and the four feed each other:
  • Kinetic Orbital Lance: Arrokoth capsules bring Primordial Tholin, Nexus-1 capsules bring Nexium. Nexus-1 can only be hit with the new Magnetar Slug (Magnetarium ingots, mass 2000 t).
  • Stellar Containment Chamber: a magnetar starquake drops 4 Magnetar Crystals, a collapse drops 64 Degenerate Core Matter. Each 60 s of magnetar field uses one Forgecore plate from the Mass Injector; without one the field drops and the crust takes 10% damage.
  • Antimatter Collider Ring: the Neutronium Magnet proposal needs 1024 fine Nexium wire in the input buses (used when it completes).
  • Dimensional Rift Gate: each biome drops one exclusive material (Prismatium, Chronomercury, Forgecore, Vivispore, Abyssal Antimatter, Precursor Residue, Void Ash). From depth 40, each Depth Anchor also uses one Contained X-Nexus.
  • Endgame recipes now use them: antiproton cells in the Cosmic Neutronium and Infinity antimatter fuel rods and the Forge of Gods siphon casing; Higgs, top and Prismatium in the Gravitational Lens; X-Nexus and the Rift Singularity in the Forge of Gods controller; Degenerate Core Matter, Chronomercury, Void Ash and the Rift Singularity in Eye of Harmony field generators from the Advanced tier (lower tiers unchanged, since the Rift Gate is built with them and runs on SpaceTime); Primordial Tholin, Precursor Residue and Vivispore in Forge of Gods casings.
  • Default construction recipes for the four originals, their special hatches, Rift Probe, Depth Anchor, Target Cartridges and the structure blocks that had none (Radiant Naquadah Alloy Casing, Precision Field Sync Casing, Nanite Shielding Glass, Degenerate Matter Core), plus a UIV route for Cosmic Neutronium Borosilicate Glass. Only GTCEu and GTNA items; a modpack can replace them by id.
  • New processing: Nexium and Forgecore ingots (blast furnace), Nexium fine wire, Forgecore plates, Magnetarium (mixer + blast furnace).
  • Field manual: new Endgame chapter and two lore pages for each original (en, pt_br, zh_cn).

docs.title: Item effects (RenderBlender no longer needed)
docs.text:
• GTNA now draws its own item effects: gtna:halo, gtna:glow_edge, gtna:cosmic, gtna:eternal and gtna:unstable model loaders, with a new procedural shader and new halo textures. RenderBlender is no longer used.
  • Fixes material icons (ingots, plates, dusts, gears, wires, gems of 56 GTNA material sets) showing as missing textures when RenderBlender was not installed (0.5.4–0.5.5). Icons now always render; the effect is drawn on top.
  • KubeJS: GTNAClientEvents.itemEffects (client scripts) adds, replaces or removes effects per item or per GTCEu material. Example in examples/kubejs/client_scripts/gtna_item_effects.js.
  • Client config: toggle halos, glow edges and shader effects, and set the animation speed.

docs.title: New multiblocks (GTO)
docs.text:
• Large Incubator: Incubator with Parallel Hatch; the glass tier caps the voltage tier, and the cleanroom filters set the filter tier a recipe may ask for (filter_casing recipe data: 1 plain, 2 sterile).
  • Kerr-Newman Homogenizer: Mixer running several recipes at once (Thread Hatch), Parallel and laser hatches.
  • Nyarlathotep's Tentacle: Assembly Line running several recipes at once with coil parallel and an Optical Data Reception Hatch.
  • Giant Sintering Array (new gtna:sintering_furnace type): coil temperature gate, parallel 4^glass tier.
  • Integrated Vapor Deposition System (new gtna:chemical_vapor_deposition and gtna:physical_vapor_deposition types): several recipes at once, parallel 4^glass tier.
  • Reaction Furnace (new gtna:reaction_furnace type): coil furnace like the Electric Blast Furnace, with an upgrade module that unlocks the Parallel and Accelerate hatches.

  • Dyson Sphere Launch Silo and Receiving Station (new gtna:dyson_sphere type, Dyson Swarm Module item): the silo puts swarm modules in orbit of its planet, the station turns them into laser power, needing computation and liquid helium; the swarm takes damage over time.

  • Space Elevator with the Assembler Module and Resource Collection Module (new gtna:assembler_module, gtna:miner_module and gtna:drilling_module types; Nanotube Spool and Space Drones MK I–VI): above ZPM, with computation and 256 Nanotube Spools, the elevator powers up to twelve modules; the Power Module MK (I–V) sets their parallel 4^(MK - 1) and which Assembler Module recipes they may run. The Resource Collection Module mines 20 asteroid ore mixes and collects 11 gases with drones and rocket fuel.

docs.title: Bose-Einstein Condensate (GTNH)
docs.text:
• Five multiblocks on a physical condensate network: the Entanglement Apparatus turns molten metals and fluids into 19 kinds of entangled condensate; the Containment Field stores it (field strength = capacity and EU/t, voided on power loss); the Maxwell Gate lets it flow one way, with filters; the Observation Array feeds nanites, EU and condensate to its Teleportation Nodes, which craft the Condensate Assembly recipes step by step, one nanite tier per item slot.
  • Bose-Einstein Condensate Conduit (dye it to split networks) and its casing; BEC Hatch, Nanite Containment Bus, Line-Of-Sight Connector Hatch (with the beam), Nanite Tier Detector, Condensate Detector and Teleportation Node Controller hatches; the BEC casings; 28 metamaterials and the Transdimensional Alignment Matrix.
  • Every GTNH BEC recipe whose output exists in GTNA, including the BEC casings and the Godforge and Eye of Harmony parts. The Singularity Shielding Casing and the Medial and Central Graviton Flow Modulators now come only from the BEC, as in GTNH; their temporary assembly-line recipes are gone.
  • New materials: Bedrockium, Tairitsu, Inactive and Boundless Cosmic Solder.

docs.title: Nano Forge
docs.text: • Tier 4: the MagMatter extension (GTNH structure with its own casings) and MagMatter Nanites. With a nanite equal to the recipe's output in an input bus, the forge drains all molten MagMatter from its hatches for extra parallel and a shorter duration, as in GTNH.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Structure check (the controller's refresh button): when the machine is formed but an optional GTNA module is not, the message now says the machine works and only the module is incomplete. It used the same "Structure incomplete" text as a broken structure, so a formed Electric Blast Furnace looked broken (player report on 0.5.2 and 0.5.5).
  • Kinetic Orbital Lance: capsules return in 30 · ln(1 + d / 50) seconds (about a minute from Nexus-1 instead of 231 hours; capsules already in flight are shortened); energy is a direct draw on the owner's Nexus network and shows in the Nexus terminal; the shot effect ends when the machine is switched off; the Magnetar Slug has its name in every language.
  • Antimatter Collider Ring: accepts up to two input buses (the Neutronium Magnet's Nexium wire goes there).
  • SpaceTime block and frame were invisible: 14 material-set block models lacked the forge:composite loader.

docs.title: Original materials: textures and halos
docs.text:
• The 12 materials of the originals have 32×32 animated textures (48 frames, with a short event per material) and their own 128×128 animated halo: field lines, a comet, pulsar beams, a compression vortex, iron filings, spectral rays, a clock, a corona, spore tendrils, dark tentacles, a nanite swarm and an ash sink. Halos sit on the main forms only (ingot, gem, dust, plate, rod, fine wire) and stay within the slot.
  • JEI/EMI info pages for the originals' exclusive materials and items (en, pt_br, zh_cn).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• New GameTests: every GTCEu multiblock forms from its own preview with GTNA loaded (71 machines); the EBF stays formed without its optional module; the lance's bank is paid from the Nexus network, exactly, and stops on an empty network.
  • New unit tests: material-set models (composite loader, missing textures, animated strips without .mcmeta) and the originals' lang keys in en_us, pt_br and zh_cn, including the keys built from enums.

docs.title: Other
docs.text:
• Tiered glass: any of 13 glasses (Tempered, MV, through Cosmic Neutronium Borosilicate, MAX) in structures that read a glass tier; all glass of one structure must match. Six GTO borosilicate glasses added (Titanium, Tritanium, Enderium, Quarks, Draconium, Cosmic Neutronium).
  • New GTO casings: Shielded Accelerator, Bioactive Mechanical Casing, Advanced Fusion Coil, UHV Accelerator Electromagnetic Coil, Uruium Coil Block, Spacetime Assembly Line Casing, Quark Pipe, Space Elevator Internal Support and Support, Space Elevator Power Modules MK I–V, Dyson Deployment Magnet, Core and Casing.
  • Recipe types left empty where GTO's recipes need GTO-only materials (sintering, vapor deposition, reaction furnace); packs add their own through KubeJS.
  • GTO's Dimensional Bridge Casing is GTNA's Spatial Casing (the old dimensional_bridge_casing id already migrates to it).
  • Not ported: GTO's Radiation Hatch (Large Incubator), Suprachronal and Circuit Assembly Line modes (Nyarlathotep), the Kerr-Newman black-hole effect (closed GTOLib), the Machine Access Link.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Crash on launch with JEI 15.32 and newer: client.UniversiumJeiFluidMixin targeted the old FluidTankRenderer.drawTiledSprite signature (JEI 15.32 added a TilingDirection parameter). There is now one injection per signature, each with its exact descriptor and optional, so the Universium fluid overlay works with any JEI 15.x. GTNA now builds against JEI 15.62.0.219.
  • The same safeguard for the other viewer-dependent injections: the Eye of Harmony tab sizing in EMI (setPage) and the stale-slot guard of GTCEu's JEI multiblock pages.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Brazilian Portuguese (pt_br) translation completed: the 313 keys that were still missing (pattern buffer, structure checks, overclock and accelerate hatches, terminal, research, materials, multi-plates and creative tabs) are now translated.

docs.title: Faster previews of huge multiblocks
docs.text: • The cached scene of LDLib (EMI/JEI multiblock previews and structure GUIs) is now compiled off-thread in batches of 4,096 blocks, each in its own vertex buffer, and drawn as batches finish. Very large structures no longer overflow a single buffer or stall until the whole structure is built. Technique from GTLCore (LGPL-3.0).

docs.title: Other
docs.text:
• New researchTree gameplay option (default on): turning it off removes the research tree key, screen and commands, for packs without research nodes.
  • Simplified Chinese (zh_cn) translation.

docs.title: Debug parts for testing (creative only, no recipes)
docs.text:
• Debug Energy Hatch and Debug Laser Target Hatch: always full. Their GUI works like the GTCEu creative energy container (and the GTMThings creative hatches): tier selector, free voltage field, amperage with -/+ buttons and an on/off switch. The laser hatch starts at 4096 A. Any change re-forms the multiblock at once.
  • Debug Input Bus and Debug Input Hatch: mark items or fluids in their 3x3 ghost slots; recipes get endless amounts and nothing is consumed. Both keep the circuit slot.
  • Debug Energy Cover: keeps the energy buffer of any GregTech machine full.
  • All of them can be turned off with the debugParts hatch toggle in the config.

docs.title: ME Export Buffer
docs.text: • The GUI now shows 9 item rows and 9 fluid rows side by side (it showed 3 of each). The buffer itself already held any number of item and fluid types.

docs.title: ⚠️ Personal Space moved to ModernSpace
docs.text:
• Personal Space is no longer part of GTNA. It now lives in its own mod, ModernSpace. GTNA no longer depends on Infiniverse.
  • Keep your personal dimensions: install ModernSpace (0.3.1 or later) together with this GTNA version. The first time an old world opens, ModernSpace imports it automatically: dimensions, settings, portals, players inside a personal dimension and portal items. The files it changes are backed up with a .modernspace_backup suffix.
  • Without ModernSpace, old portals disappear and the personal dimensions stop loading. Their folders stay in the save.

docs.title: New multiblocks (ported from GTOCore)
docs.text:
• Processing: High Energy Laser Lathe, Extreme Compressor, Gemini Containment System (packer), Giant Electrochemical Workstation, Heavy Rolling (bender), Hand of Arachne (loom), Desulfurizer (with an optional extension structure), Rare Earth Centrifugal, Lightning Rod (arc generator), PCB Factory (three structure tiers, chosen with a screwdriver), Compound Extreme Cooling Unit (vacuum freezer, atomization and, on its larger structure, plasma condensing), Dimensional Focus Engraving Array, Star Ultimate Material Forge Factory and Space Probe Receiver (works only in space).
  • Plasma and power: Hyperdimensional Plasma Fusion Core (runs Plasma Forge recipes in parallel), Hyper Reactor and Advanced Hyper Reactor (booster plasmas set per recipe), Fuel Cell Generator (absorption, transfer and release modes with membrane electrodes and redox-flow electrolytes).
  • Research: Supercomputing Center (three tiers: HPCA, NICH and GWCA components, MFPC coolant in the new Thermal Conductor Hatch), Data Center and Analysis & Research Center.
  • New recipe types, casings, glasses, materials and parts that come with them. Some GTOCore recipe types ship empty (or with only the recipes whose ingredients exist outside GTOCore) so modpacks can fill them.
  • A new check makes sure every recipe type, block and item has an English and Portuguese name and a model.

docs.title: Multiblock tooltips
docs.text:
• Every GTNA multiblock now uses the same tooltip layout: machine type, a flavor line, a short description and colored bullet lines for bonuses, numbers and restrictions, followed by the source addon.
  • Several tooltip numbers were wrong and now match the machines (Large Steam Circuit Assembler parallel, Large Steam Centrifuge, Thermal Centrifuge and Alloy Smelter speed, Steam Elevator Apiary and Beacon modules).

docs.title: Batteries
docs.text: • The Really, Extremely, Insanely and Mega Ultimate Batteries are now rechargeable batteries (UEV, UIV, UXV and OpV), tagged gtceu:batteries/<tier>.
Big endgame update. Changes below are relative to 0.5.1.

docs.title: ⚠️ Dependencies
docs.text:
• New required dependency: Infiniverse 1.0.0.5 or newer (used by Personal Space dimensions). It is not bundled; install it alongside GTNA.
  • Optional: Ad Astra (planet ores, planet simulations in the Eye of Harmony, planet dimension icons) and SGJourney.
  • Tested with GTCEu 7.5.3.

docs.title: New multiblocks
docs.text:
• Forge of Gods (GTNH): controller with ring sub-structures, upgrade tree, milestones, fuel and battery, cosmetics, star and beam rendering, and the Smelting, Molten, Plasma and Exotic modules. The Plasma Module now also covers the GT++ metals (Celestial Tungsten, Astral Titanium, Hypogen, Rhugnor, Six-Phased Copper…).
  • Dimensionally Transcendent Plasma Forge (GTNH): coil heat, EBF-style overclock and the catalyst discount after long continuous runs.
  • Transcendent Plasma Mixer (GTNH): powered only by the owner's wireless network; the full cost is paid when a recipe starts.
  • Nano Forge tiers 1–3 (GTNH) with 11 nanites. The tier nanite goes in an input bus (GTCEu controllers have no slot).
  • Advanced Fusion Reactor (GTO) with four tier extensions and an overclock extension. It replaces GTNH Fusion Mk4/Mk5.
  • ME Export Buffer (GTMThings style).

docs.title: Eye of Harmony
docs.text:
• Planet simulations: Nether, End and, with Ad Astra, Moon, Mars, Venus, Mercury and Glacio, each with its own Planet Block, rocket tier and ore catalogue.
  • KubeJS support for adding and editing simulation programs.
  • Recipe viewers: reworked JEI page that matches the EMI layout (separate item and fluid grids, one page per simulation, the window grows to fit).
  • Recipes: controller, casings and field generators now use fluids, as in GTNH.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• Forge of Gods material chain ported from GTNH: Creon, Mellion, Transcendent Metal, Six-Phased Copper, Hypogen, Rhugnor, Phonon Medium, Tengam, UIV/UMV superconductors, Infinity, Eternity, Shirabon, Dimensionally Shifted Superfluid, the Excited catalysts and more, with default recipes.
  • GTNH Forge of Gods components: Stable Boson Containment Unit, heat capacitors, Thermal Superconductor, Tengam Electromagnet, Graviton Anomaly, Cosmic Fabric Manipulator, Force Field Glass, Field Restriction Coil, Raw Tesseract, ZPM3–ZPM6 batteries. The Forge of Gods progression and upgrade costs now follow GTNH.
  • New circuits: Optical (UV–UIV) and Exotic (UHV–UXV) circuit families. OpV/MAX circuits are left to modpacks.
  • Recipes GTCEu lacks: default recipes for UHV–OpV components (motors, pistons, pumps, conveyors, robot arms, emitters, sensors, field generators), UEV–MAX machine casings and energy hatches, and UU Matter. All of them can be replaced with KubeJS.
  • Ad Astra planets: ore veins, and proper dimension icons in GTCEu dimension conditions (World Data Scanner, ore veins).
  • Hatches: high-tier module hatches and wireless hatch recipes.
  • Restricted parts: recipes for the output-boost and infinite-input parts. They only act on recipes of their own tier.
  • Flotation line: the full reagent chain (carbon disulfide, ethylates, xanthates, turpentine).
  • Removed: Matrix Modules I–IV and the Nexus Hypercore Casing.

docs.title: Personal Space
docs.text:
• Port of the GTNH PersonalSpace dimensions:
  • configurable worldgen and sky;
  • editor GUI;
  • portal and portal book;
  • /pspace commands.
  • The portal now appears in the creative tab and has an LV recipe made with normal obsidian.

docs.title: GTO machinery and balance
docs.text:
• GTO machines: Blaze Blast Furnace, Cold Ice Freezer, Chemical Plant, Mega Alloy Blast Smelter, ISA Mill, Rocket and Supercritical turbines, Industrial Flotation Cell, Vacuum Drying Furnace, Component Assembler and Component Assembly Line.
  • Dehydrator family: full LV–OpV set.
  • Wireless: energy HUD overlay.
  • Balance profiles: configurable profiles for the Universal Factory, Nexus wireless loss and ME Pattern Buffer capacity.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Missing names: item and block names no longer disappear (two language generators were overwriting each other).
  • Material textures: icon sets for Hypogen, Chromatic Glass, Dragonblood and Black Dwarf Matter, plus extra plate forms for the custom sets.
  • Fluid textures: original textures for Infinity, Eternity, Hypogen, Chromatic Glass, Rhugnor, Dragonblood, Primordial Matter, the Phonon fluids and Stable Baryonic Matter. Fluids with no texture get their own colour instead of white.
  • Item textures: glowstone nanite animation fixed; ZPM4–ZPM6 batteries are now tinted per tier.
  • Tooltips: the new multiblocks use the standard tooltip format with source attribution.
  • Nano Forge: tier 2 and 3 extensions now use the Assembly Line Casing, as in GTNH.
  • ME Pattern Buffer: upgrades no longer spill stored patterns or render invisibly.
  • Dead-end recipes: several were found and fixed by a new recipe reachability check.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Bose-Einstein Condensate machines are not ported yet. Until then, the Singularity Shielding Casing and the Medial/Central Graviton Flow Modulators use provisional Assembly Line recipes, and the DTPF's Transdimensional Alignment Matrix / Convergence is unavailable.
  • Nano Forge tier 4 is not ported yet.

docs.title: Corrected JAR
docs.text:
• Fixed production startup crashes in the GTCEu module-tooltip and AE2 crafting-confirmation mixins. Both now recognize the Minecraft 1.20.1 runtime method names, and missing injection targets cannot stop the game from loading.
  • Reduced repeated structure checks while the Nexus Terminal builds the Nexus ME Hypercore. The target structure is checked once at the end of the build. The in-world build time still needs confirmation with the corrected JAR.
  • Re-tested startup in a Prism Launcher instance with GTCEu 7.5.3, AE2 15.4.10 and KubeJS 2001.6.5-build.26. The full validation gate passed with 60/60 GameTests.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Ported four GTOCore multiblocks: Generator Array, Fishing Ground, Evaporation Plant and Greenhouse, with their structures, recipes, casings and English/Portuguese tooltips. The Evaporation Plant also has its titanium auxiliary tower.
  • Generator Array supports its eligible GTCEu generators and can send power to the Nexus Flux Matrix in wireless mode. Fishing Ground includes its bait, water and circuit based catches.
  • Added automated formation, recipe, tooltip and behavior checks for the new machines.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Removed Nexus Flux Matrix Safe Mode. Valid energy withdrawals can drain the network to zero; old SafeMode save data is ignored and no longer written.
  • Wireless Steam Hatches now declare steam specific abilities only. They no longer fill general fluid hatch slots in electric multiblocks.
  • Clarified Evaporation Plant hatch placement: one fluid input and one or two energy inputs go in the base; fluid outputs go in the tower stages. Fluid hatch tier is unrestricted.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Prevented a startup crash with KubeJS 2001.6.5-build.26 caused by the GTNA DataGenerator mixin targeting a missing method name. The injection is now optional and handles the runtime method name used by Minecraft 1.20.1.
  • Greenhouse sunlight detection now responds to an opaque roof cover and recovers when it is removed.
  • Revised the four ported machines' tooltips to remove duplicate descriptions and preserve source attribution and relevant mechanics in both supported languages.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: • Passed the full formatting, compilation, unit test, GameTest server and data generation gate. The GameTest suite passed all 60 required tests, including a MAX fluid output hatch in a valid Evaporation Plant tower stage.

This release expands steam and ore processing, adds multiblock modules and strengthens AE2 autocrafting. It also includes the Structure Terminal improvements, ME Pattern Buffer fixes, tooltips and automated tests recorded in the continuity ledger.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Electric Blast Furnace module: a GTNA sub-pattern registered for gtceu:electric_blast_furnace that adds Parallel / Overclock / Accelerate / Thread hatches to the furnace.
  • KubeJS support for sub-patterns: the GTNAServerEvents.subPatterns server event lets modpack creators add module/extension structures to any multiblock (new or existing), unlocking new abilities (see docs/roadmap/sub-patterns.md).
  • Sub-pattern (module/extension) mechanic (ISubPatternMachine + a MultiblockControllerMachine mixin): a multiblock can be extended by additional structures attached to the same controller, whose parts are merged in to unlock new abilities (e.g. Parallel / Accelerate hatches). Ported in the spirit of GTOCore's addSubPattern.
  • Liquefaction Furnace (GTOCore port, LGPLv3): a coil multiblock that melts an item into a fluid, with a stainless-steel extension tower as its sub-pattern.
  • Thermal Power Pump (GTOCore port, LGPLv3): a primitive no-energy multiblock that condenses steam into water at a biome-dependent rate (rain +50%; the Nether produces nothing).
  • Brick Kiln (GTOCore port, LGPLv3): a primitive no-energy multiblock that fires bricks and ceramics from compressed clay + coal (parallel 4), closing the ULV era.
  • Integrated Ore Processor (GTLCore port, LGPLv3): the 6×12×11 stainless/HSSE multiblock that collapses the macerate → wash → thermal/sift/centrifuge chain into one recipe per circuit.
  • Advanced Integrated Ore Processor (GTLCore/TST port, LGPLv3): the 32×12×15 laser-powered, effectively unlimited-parallel endgame version.
  • Faithful integrated ore processing recipes: one recipe per circuit 1..7 for both raw ore and stone ore, with the real per-stage byproducts, the material's own washing fluid (distilled water, mercury, sodium persulfate, ...) and GTLCore's durations/EUt. The multiplier is configurable (gtna/balance/machines.json → integratedOreMultiplier, default 4 = GTLCore parity).
  • Craft recipes for the two new multiblocks: Assembler (EV) for the Integrated Ore Processor and Assembly Line (UHV) for the Advanced Integrated Ore Processor.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• gtna:ore_processing now uses GTLCore's IO sizes (2 item in / 9 item out / 1 fluid in).
  • Steam Ore Processing Module: no longer consumes lubricant; it consumes the washing fluid of the matching integrated recipe (circuit 1 needs none; 2/3/4 distilled water; 5/6/7 the ore's fluid). Its input filter now only accepts ore/crushed prefixes, not ingots.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Steam Ore Processing Module returned the raw ore unchanged: the recipe lookup passed Ingredient.of(stack) to GT's recipe DB, which does not expand the item's tags, so tag-based ore recipes were never found. It now passes the ItemStack (like GT's own SmartItemFilter).
  • Addon logo now shows in every GTNA multiblock UI: a client-only mixin on GTCEu's FancyMachineUIWidget covers the electric/no-energy/fancy-steam controllers, and the two custom 310×270 UIs (Nexus ME Hypercore, Nexus Flux Matrix) got an explicit logo.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Universal Factory (GTNA-native port of GTLsupb, LGPLv3): 32 recipe types, cross-recipe threads, warmup/overload/batch processing, and the new universal_factory_casing.
  • Primitive Stone Furnace (GTLsupb port): zero-energy multiblock that smelts with effectively unlimited threads and parallel.
  • Thread Hatch wiring: the Industrial Slaughterhouse and the Dimensionally Transcendent Dirt Forge are now on the multiple-recipes base and accept the Thread Hatch.
  • Source attribution in tooltips: ported machines now show Source: <addon> (GTO, GTNL, TST, GTLsupb, GTOEPP), and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md documents the license of every source.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Accelerate Hatch: penalty now uses the recipe's pre-overclock tier (GTO parity — a low-tier recipe in a high-tier machine is not punished), the amount is player-configurable, and the tooltips follow the GTO wording.
  • Overclock Hatch: parity with GTOCore (100 / (tier - 6) %, configurable).
  • Industrial Slaughterhouse migrated to WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine.
  • Dimensionally Transcendent Dirt Forge migrated to the multiple-recipes base as a zero-energy machine (getMaxParallel() = 524288, 1-tick duration).
  • Large Steam Solar Boiler is the single solar boiler; the duplicate Mega Pressure Solar Boiler (class, config, balance, lang, docs and recipes) was removed and the Hyper Pressure Reactor recipe now uses the large one.
  • Configurable amounts for the Accelerate/Overclock/Thread hatches, with GTO-style tooltips.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Output Boost double application (M→M²) on the multiple-recipes base.
  • Pattern buffer crashes: tier-index guard in WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine display text, NPE guard in PatternSlotResolver, and scaled-input push in ParallelPatternDetails.
  • Dedicated server crash: two client-only leaks in common code.
  • Jade config translation crash for the pattern buffer provider.
  • Nine config options that rendered as raw lang keys.
  • Zero-energy parallel computation bypassing GT's ParallelLogic.getMaxByInput.

docs.title: Contribute
docs.text:
GTNA is open source and developed in the GTInfinityAscension organisation. You can help without writing code.

How Where Report a bug or a wrong page issues Translate the mod or this wiki Translating Fix a page the edit button at the top of every page Write code Development setup, Architecture, Contributing code Follow what is coming Roadmap

Please read the organisation's Code of Conduct and AI policy first.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
GTNA is a GTCEu addon (GTNAGTAddon) with mod id gtna, main class com.raishxn.gtna.GTNACORE.

Package Contents api public interfaces and helpers for addons; see the Java API common.data registration: machines (GTNAMachines, GTNAMachines2, GTNAMegaMachines…), blocks, items, materials, recipe types, sources (GTNASources) common.machine machine classes: multiblock/steam, electric, energy, noenergy, godforge, originals, part (hatches, AE2 parts) data datagen: lang (GTNALangProvider), recipes (data/recipe) config ConfigHolder (gtna.yaml) and GTNABalance (config/gtna/balance/*.json) integration AE2, JEI, EMI, Jade, KubeJS, FTB mixin GTCEu and AE2 mixins (auxiliary modules, hatch behaviour, previews) client, network rendering, screens, HUDs, packets research the research engine gametest GameTests, run with runGameTestServer

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Ported machines keep the source's structure, behaviour and tooltips; the source is declared once in GTNASources and shown as the last tooltip line.
  • Every visible name exists in en_us (generated), pt_br and zh_cn.
  • Never reference JEI types outside integration/jei and never reference net.minecraft.client from common code: EMI-only clients and dedicated servers must load the mod. Tests enforce both.
  • Energy and fluid payments are simulate → charge → execute; balances never go negative.
  • Organisation-wide rules (file size, trilingual key comments) are in the developer conventions.

docs.title: Contributing code
docs.text:
The organisation-wide guide is the CONTRIBUTING of GTInfinityAscension. The short version for GTNA:

  1. For anything larger than a bug fix, open an issue first. Balance and progression changes need the author's approval.
  2. Fork, branch from main, one topic per pull request.
  3. Every new machine, item or recipe ships with names in en_us, pt_br and zh_cn.
  4. Add or update GameTests. A new multiblock needs a test that it forms and a negative test (it must not form or run when it should not).
  5. Run ./gradlew spotlessCheck compileJava runUnitTests runGameTestServer runData and say in the pull request how you tested in game.
  6. Commit messages and changelog entries are in English.
  7. Ports keep their source credit: add the machine to GTNASources and follow the licence notes in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• JDK 17
  • Git
  • An IDE with Gradle support; IntelliJ IDEA with the Minecraft Development plugin works well. The code uses Lombok.

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/GTInfinityAscension/GregTech-Nexus-Addon.git
cd GregTech-Nexus-Addon
./gradlew build          # compile and package
./gradlew runClient      # start a development client
./gradlew runData        # regenerate lang files, models and recipes

Before a pull request, run the same checks as the maintainers:

./gradlew spotlessCheck compileJava runUnitTests runGameTestServer runData
  • ./gradlew spotlessApply fixes the formatting.
  • Create run/eula.txt with eula=true before the first GameTest run.
  • runGameTestServer can exit with 0 even when a recipe fails to parse: search the log for Parsing error loading recipe gtna:.

docs.title: Wiki
docs.text:
pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-static-i18n
mkdocs serve

The catalog needs the datagen dump: run ./gradlew runData, then python3 tools/wiki/generate_machine_pages.py (add --no-render to keep the existing images). See Translating for the other generators.

docs.title: Translating
docs.text:
Translations are welcome, for the mod and for this wiki. Today GTNA ships English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Simplified Chinese. A new language starts small and can grow page by page: anything not translated yet falls back to English.

Before a big translation, open an issue or say hello on Discord so two people do not translate the same thing.

docs.title: The mod
docs.text:
Every name and tooltip in the game comes from one JSON file per language:

src/main/resources/assets/gtna/lang/<locale>.json      e.g. ru_ru.json, de_de.json, ja_jp.json
  1. Fork the repository and create the file for your locale. Use the Minecraft locale code (ru_ru, es_es, fr_fr…).
  2. Copy keys from the English source and translate the values. The full English file is generated by ./gradlew runData into src/generated/resources/assets/gtna/lang/en_us.json; pt_br.json and zh_cn.json in the same folder as yours are good references.
  3. Keep the § colour codes and the %s placeholders exactly as they are.

  4. Check what is still missing:

    python3 tools/check_lang_parity.py --locale ru_ru

  5. Open a pull request. Partial files are fine; missing keys show in English.

docs.title: This wiki
docs.text:
The wiki is built with MkDocs Material and mkdocs-static-i18n. Each page is a Markdown file in docs/; a translation is the same file with a language suffix:

docs/gameplay/systems/bec.md       English (the source)
docs/gameplay/systems/bec.pt.md    Português
docs/gameplay/systems/bec.zh.md    简体中文
docs/gameplay/systems/bec.ru.md    your translation

docs.title: Small fixes
docs.text: Every page has an edit button (the pencil at the top). It opens the file on GitHub, where you can propose a change without installing anything.

docs.title: A new language
docs.text:
1. Add the language to mkdocs.yml, under plugins → i18n → languages, next to pt and zh:

    - locale: ru
  name: Русский
  build: true
  nav_translations:
    Home: Главная
    Machines: Машины

  2. Translate pages by creating <page>.ru.md next to the English file. Start with index, getting-started/ and the pages you use most. Keep links and image paths as they are: they point to the same files in every language.

  3. Some pages are generated, so do not edit them by hand:

    Pages Generator Where the text comes from gameplay/machines/catalog/* tools/wiki/generate_machine_pages.py the mod's lang files, so translate the mod first gameplay/materials/index* tools/wiki/material_pages.py the mod's lang files and the intro inside the script gameplay/systems/forge-of-gods*, eye-of-harmony* tools/wiki/system_pages.py text dictionaries inside the script roadmap/index* tools/wiki/roadmap_page.py text dictionaries inside the script

    To add a language to a generator, add an entry to its language list and its text dictionary, then run it.

  4. Preview locally:

    pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-static-i18n
mkdocs serve

    Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ru/. mkdocs build --strict must finish without warnings before the pull request.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
• Write the way a player talks; short sentences beat long ones.
  • Use the item and machine names that the game shows in your language. If the mod has no translation for a name yet, keep the English name.
  • Numbers, formulas, config keys and ids stay exactly as in the English page.

docs.title: KubeJS API
docs.text:
GTNA works with KubeJS out of the box: install KubeJS and the bindings below are there. Complete, runnable examples are in examples/kubejs/ in the repository.

Feature Script folder What for gtna:multiple_recipes startup_scripts a new multiblock that runs several recipes at once GTNAServerEvents.subPatterns server_scripts auxiliary modules for any multiblock GTNAStartupEvents.eyeOfHarmony startup_scripts add or remove Eye of Harmony planets GTNAClientEvents.itemEffects client_scripts halos, glow edges and shaders on item icons GTNAPartAbility any GTNA hatch abilities for structure patterns

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
GTNA's recipe types are GTCEu recipe types in the gtna namespace, so the usual GTCEu KubeJS syntax works with event.recipes.gtna:

ServerEvents.recipes(event => {
  event.recipes.gtna.hydraulic_manufacturing('kubejs:my_piston')
    .itemInputs('4x gtceu:bronze_plate')
    .itemOutputs('gtna:hydraulic_piston')
    .duration(100)
    .EUt(16)
})

The recipe type of every machine is listed on its catalog page. The research engine can gate any recipe id behind a research node from a datapack.

docs.title: Multiple-recipes machines
docs.text:
gtna:multiple_recipes builds a multiblock on WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine, the same base as the Industrial Slaughterhouse and the Integrated Ore Processor. It uses the GTCEu multiblock builder, and with a Thread Hatch it runs several different recipes at the same time.

GTCEuStartupEvents.registry('gtceu:machine', event => {
  event.create('my_assembly_hall', 'gtna:multiple_recipes')
    .recipeType('gtceu:assembler')
    .rotationState(RotationState.NON_Y_AXIS)
    .appearanceBlock(GTBlocks.CASING_STEEL_SOLID)
    .pattern(definition => FactoryBlockPattern.start()
      .aisle('CCCCC', 'CCCCC', 'CCCCC')
      .aisle('CCCCC', 'C###C', 'CCCCC')
      .aisle('CCCCC', 'C###C', 'CCCCC')
      .aisle('CCCCC', 'C###C', 'CCCCC')
      .aisle('CCCCC', 'CC~CC', 'CCCCC')
      .where('~', Predicates.controller(Predicates.blocks(definition.get())))
      .where('C', Predicates.blocks(GTBlocks.CASING_STEEL_SOLID.get())
        .or(Predicates.autoAbilities(definition.getRecipeTypes()))
        .or(Predicates.abilities(PartAbility.MAINTENANCE).setExactLimit(1))
        .or(Predicates.abilities(GTNAPartAbility.PARALLEL_CONTROL_HATCH).setMaxGlobalLimited(1))
        .or(Predicates.abilities(GTNAPartAbility.THREAD_HATCH).setMaxGlobalLimited(1))
        .or(Predicates.abilities(GTNAPartAbility.ACCELERATE_HATCH).setMaxGlobalLimited(1))
        .or(Predicates.abilities(GTNAPartAbility.OVERCLOCK_HATCH).setMaxGlobalLimited(1)))
      .where('#', Predicates.air())
      .build())
    .workableCasingModel('gtceu:block/casings/solid/machine_casing_solid_steel',
      'gtceu:block/multiblock/implosion_compressor')
})

docs.title: Auxiliary modules
docs.text:
Adds an optional extra structure to an existing multiblock, GTNA's or another mod's. The pattern is checked from the controller's position and facing; the parts found in it join the machine. See Modules for what players see.

GTNAServerEvents.subPatterns(event => {
  // a three-block column beside the Integrated Ore Processor; the middle block may be an input bus
  event.add('gtna:integrated_ore_processor', definition => FactoryBlockPattern.start()
    .aisle('   A', 'C  A', '   A')
    .where('C', Predicates.controller(Predicates.blocks(definition.get())))
    .where('A', Predicates.blocks(GTBlocks.CASING_STAINLESS_CLEAN.get())
      .or(Predicates.abilities(PartAbility.IMPORT_ITEMS).setMaxGlobalLimited(1)))
    .where(' ', Predicates.any())
    .build(), 'gtna.machine.auxiliary_module.kubejs.item_import')
})
Overload Meaning add(machineId, factory) registers the module add(machineId, factory, descriptionKey) adds a tooltip line from a translation key add(machineId, factory, descriptionKey, speedBonus, perfectOverclock) on multiple-recipes machines, the bonus applies only while this module is formed: 2.0 halves the duration (combined cap 1024×); true enables perfect overclock when no Overclock Hatch overrides the curve

docs.title: Eye of Harmony planets
docs.text:
GTNAStartupEvents.eyeOfHarmony(event => {
  // add(planetItem, dimension, rocketTier[, stoneDust])
  event.add('kubejs:titan_planet_block', 'mymod:titan', 5)
  event.remove('gtna:eye_of_harmony_planet_glacio')
})

The products are the GTCEu ore veins registered in that dimension, scaled with the GTNH rules for the rocket tier (0–9). Formulas are on the Eye of Harmony page.

docs.title: Item effects
docs.text:
GTNAClientEvents.itemEffects(event => {
  event.material('gtna:advanced_nitinol').halo(0xFF66CCFF, 8).pulse(true)
  event.item('minecraft:nether_star').cosmic().colors(0xFF050418, 0xFF7FD4FF).glowEdge(0xFFFFAA00, 1.5)
  event.item('minecraft:amethyst_shard').eternal().mask('gtna:mask/cosmic').speed(0.5)
})

Every method is listed on the Item effects page. The script runs again on every F3+T.

docs.title: GTNAPartAbility
docs.text:
Binding Hatch GTNAPartAbility.THREAD_HATCH Thread Hatch GTNAPartAbility.ACCELERATE_HATCH Accelerate Hatch GTNAPartAbility.OVERCLOCK_HATCH Overclock Hatch GTNAPartAbility.OUTPUT_BOOST_HATCH Output Boost Hatch GTNAPartAbility.PARALLEL_CONTROL_HATCH GTCEu's Parallel Control Hatch, GTNA's UHV+ hatches included (PARALLEL_HATCH is an alias)

Use them in Predicates.abilities(...), usually with .setMaxGlobalLimited(1).

docs.title: Machines API
docs.text: How to make a multiblock that uses GTNA's hatches. The same machine in KubeJS is on the KubeJS API page.

docs.title: A machine with every GTNA hatch
docs.text:
WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine runs several recipes at once when a Thread Hatch is present, and applies the Accelerate and Overclock Hatches. Without that class, a Thread Hatch has no effect.

import com.gregtechceu.gtceu.GTCEu;
import com.gregtechceu.gtceu.api.data.RotationState;
import com.gregtechceu.gtceu.api.machine.MultiblockMachineDefinition;
import com.gregtechceu.gtceu.api.pattern.FactoryBlockPattern;
import com.gregtechceu.gtceu.common.data.GTBlocks;
import com.gregtechceu.gtceu.common.data.GTRecipeTypes;
import com.raishxn.gtna.api.machine.multiblock.GTNAPartAbility;
import com.raishxn.gtna.common.machine.multiblock.electric.WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine;

import static com.gregtechceu.gtceu.api.machine.multiblock.PartAbility.*;
import static com.gregtechceu.gtceu.api.pattern.Predicates.*;

public class MyMachines {

    public static final MultiblockMachineDefinition THREADED_ASSEMBLER = REGISTRATE
            .multiblock("threaded_assembler", WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine::new)
            .rotationState(RotationState.NON_Y_AXIS)
            .recipeType(GTRecipeTypes.ASSEMBLER_RECIPES)
            .appearanceBlock(GTBlocks.CASING_STEEL_SOLID)
            .pattern(definition -> FactoryBlockPattern.start()
                    .aisle("CCCCC", "CCCCC", "CCCCC")
                    .aisle("CCCCC", "C###C", "CCCCC")
                    .aisle("CCCCC", "C###C", "CCCCC")
                    .aisle("CCCCC", "C###C", "CCCCC")
                    .aisle("CCCCC", "CC~CC", "CCCCC")
                    .where('~', controller(blocks(definition.get())))
                    .where('C', blocks(GTBlocks.CASING_STEEL_SOLID.get())
                            .or(autoAbilities(definition.getRecipeTypes()))
                            .or(abilities(MAINTENANCE).setExactLimit(1))
                            .or(abilities(PARALLEL_HATCH).setMaxGlobalLimited(1))
                            .or(abilities(GTNAPartAbility.THREAD_HATCH).setMaxGlobalLimited(1))
                            .or(abilities(GTNAPartAbility.ACCELERATE_HATCH).setMaxGlobalLimited(1))
                            .or(abilities(GTNAPartAbility.OVERCLOCK_HATCH).setMaxGlobalLimited(1)))
                    .where('#', air())
                    .build())
            .workableCasingModel(GTCEu.id("block/casings/solid/machine_casing_solid_steel"),
                    GTCEu.id("block/multiblock/implosion_compressor"))
            .register();
}

WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine is in common, not api: it is stable in practice, but check the changelog when you update GTNA.

docs.title: Adding a module to an existing machine
docs.text:
GTNASubPatterns.register(new ResourceLocation("gtceu", "electric_blast_furnace"),
        definition -> FactoryBlockPattern.start()
                /* the extra structure, anchored at the controller */
                .build(),
        Component.translatable("mymod.module.tooltip"));

The module is optional for the machine, shows as an extra page in the JEI/EMI preview and lists the tooltip lines on the controller item. Java machines can also declare modules themselves by implementing ISubPatternMachine; those do not appear in the preview.

docs.title: Java or KubeJS?
docs.text: Java KubeJS Use for addons, custom logic modpacks Machine class WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine::new 'gtna:multiple_recipes' Abilities GTNAPartAbility.* GTNAPartAbility.* (binding) Recipes GTRecipeBuilder / GTNARecipeType event.recipes.gtna.<type>

docs.title: Materials API
docs.text: GTNA materials are ordinary GTCEu materials registered under the gtna namespace, so every GTCEu material tool applies: forms are generated from flags, and recipes use ChemicalHelper or tags such as forge:ingots/<material>. The materials page lists them.

docs.title: Registering a material in your addon
docs.text:
GTCEu materials are registered in the MaterialEvent of your GTCEu addon class:

public static Material MyAlloy;

public static void register() {
    MyAlloy = new Material.Builder(MyMod.id("my_alloy"))
            .ingot().fluid()
            .color(0x7FD4FF)
            .iconSet(MaterialIconSet.METALLIC)
            .components(GTMaterials.Iron, 3, GTMaterials.Copper, 1)
            .blastTemp(1200, BlastProperty.GasTier.LOW)
            .flags(MaterialFlags.GENERATE_PLATE, MaterialFlags.GENERATE_ROD, MaterialFlags.GENERATE_GEAR)
            .buildAndRegister();
}

The GTCEu documentation covers every builder option.

docs.title: Using GTNA materials
docs.text:
ItemStack plate = ChemicalHelper.get(TagPrefix.plate, GTNAMaterials.Stronze);

Turn on advanced tooltips (F3+H) to see the exact id of any material form before using it in a script.

docs.title: Icon effects
docs.text: To give your own material a halo or a shader, use the gtna:* item model loaders or the KubeJS event on the Item effects page.

docs.title: Java API
docs.text: For addons written in Java. Modpacks usually only need the KubeJS API.

docs.title: Depending on GTNA
docs.text:
Release jars are on the organisation's Maven:

repositories {
    maven { url = 'https://gtinfinityascension.github.io/maven/' }
}

dependencies {
    modImplementation("com.raishxn.gtna:gtna:<version>")
    modImplementation("com.gtinfinityascension:gtialib:<version>")
}

GTNA also needs GTCEu 7.5.3+ and Applied Energistics 2 on the classpath. See Installation for the runtime versions.

docs.title: Public packages
docs.text:
Everything under com.raishxn.gtna.api is meant for addons. Classes outside api can change without notice.

Package Main types What for api.machine.multiblock GTNAPartAbility, GTNASubPatterns, ISubPatternMachine, IGTNAModuleHost, ParallelMachine hatch abilities, auxiliary modules, parallel api.machine IThreadModifierMachine, IZeroEnergyMachine machine behaviour interfaces api.machine.feature AccelerateHatchMath, OverclockHatchMath, godforge.GodforgeMath, eyeofharmony.EyeOfHarmonyMath, pattern buffer mode interfaces the formulas behind the hatches and endgame systems; the wiki tables come from here api.capability WirelessEnergyManager, SteamWirelessNetworkManager read and change a player's Nexus EU and steam balance api.steam GTNASteamBalance scale the parallel and duration of every GTNA steam multiblock from one provider api.bec BECNetwork, CondensateType, NaniteTier the Bose-Einstein Condensate network api.render ItemEffect, ItemEffectOverrides item icon effects api.registry GTNARegistry GTNA's Registrate instance

docs.title: Part abilities
docs.text:
GTNAPartAbility holds GTNA's own slots. The common ones:

Ability Hatch THREAD_HATCH Thread Hatch; the machine also needs IThreadModifierMachine (for example WorkableElectricMultipleRecipesMachine) ACCELERATE_HATCH Accelerate Hatch OVERCLOCK_HATCH Overclock Hatch OUTPUT_BOOST_HATCH Output Boost Hatch STEAM_EXPORT_FLUIDS Wireless Steam Output Hatch

The rest (BEC_HATCH, LINE_OF_SIGHT_HATCH, TUNING_HATCH…) belong to specific GTNA machines.

The module registry moved to GTIA Lib in 0.6.1 (com.gtinfinityascension.gtialib.module.ModuleRegistry); GTNASubPatterns still works and forwards to it. Int128 and the block-position helpers moved to com.gtinfinityascension.gtialib.data.

docs.title: Machines
docs.text:
GTNA registers 170 multiblocks. Every one has a page in the catalog, generated from the mod code: a render of the structure, the in-game description, the recipe types and the block list.

Category Count Start with Steam and primitive 66 Steam age Electric processing 63 the catalog and the Industrial Slaughterhouse Power generation 10 Naquadah reactors, Nexus energy network Energy, AE2 and computation 6 ME Pattern Buffers Endgame systems 20 Forge of the Gods, Eye of Harmony GTNA originals 4 Original multiblocks Developer tools 1 the Duration Tester, for testing hatches

docs.title: Where they come from
docs.text:
Most machines are ports, credited in game on the last tooltip line and on each catalog page:

  • GT: Not Leisure (54): the large steam machines and many steam-age structures.
  • GregTech Odyssey (82) and GregTech Leisure (9): most electric and endgame multiblocks, including the Eye of Harmony and the Dyson Sphere.
  • GT: New Horizons (14): Forge of the Gods, Bose-Einstein Condensate, Nano Forge, Space Elevator.
  • Twist Space Technology: Eye of Wood.
  • GTNA originals: the four original multiblocks and several systems.

Licences and permissions are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

docs.title: Building big structures
docs.text:
• JEI/EMI shows every structure layer by layer.
  • The Nexus Structure Terminal builds a structure for you, picks coil and casing tiers, and can take blocks from an ME network.
  • Some machines accept auxiliary modules that unlock more hatches or recipe types.

docs.title: Industrial Slaughterhouse
docs.text: Virtual mob farming: the machine rolls the vanilla loot tables of the chosen mob group, with no mobs in the world. Catalog page.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Put a programmed circuit in the input bus:

Circuit Mode Mobs From EU/t Drop multiplier 1 Passive chicken, cow, pig, sheep, rabbit, horse, goat LV 1,000 \(2^{\,\text{tier} - \text{LV}}\) 2 Hostile zombie, skeleton, creeper, spider, enderman, witch, blaze MV 2,560 \(2^{\,\text{tier} - \text{MV}}\) 3 Bosses warden, wither, elder guardian ZPM 32,000 \(3^{\,\text{tier} - \text{ZPM}}\) 4 Dragon 1 Dragon Egg, 4 Dragon's Breath, 1 Dragon Head UHV 120,000 \(5^{\,\text{tier} - \text{UHV}}\)

Each run lasts 40 ticks. The tier is the machine's energy tier. Below the mode's starting tier the machine produces nothing.

docs.title: How much it drops
docs.text:
Each run repeats \(\max(1,\ (\text{tier} - 2) \times 8)\) times: once at LV and MV, 8 at HV, 16 at EV, 24 at IV and so on. Every repeat picks a random mob of the group, rolls its loot table and multiplies each drop by the mode's multiplier, capped at one stack per drop.

Tier Repeats Passive Hostile Bosses Dragon LV 1 1× — — — MV 1 2× 1× — — HV 8 4× 2× — — EV 16 8× 4× — — IV 24 16× 8× — — LuV 32 32× 16× — — ZPM 40 64× 32× 1× — UV 48 128× 64× 3× — UHV 56 256× 128× 9× 1× UEV 64 512× 256× 27× 5×

Each drop is capped at one stack (64 for most items), so above 64× the multiplier adds nothing more; the extra repeats still do. Since drops come from the real loot tables, mods and datapacks that change mob loot also change this machine.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Give it several output buses: high tiers produce many stacks per run.
  • It runs on GTNA's multiple-recipes logic and accepts the Thread, Accelerate and Overclock Hatches.
  • The GUI shows the current mode, the multiplier and the last drops.

docs.title: Naquadah reactors
docs.text:
Two generators burn naquadah fuel for EU. The Large Naquadah Reactor (UHV, port from GregTech Odyssey) comes first; the Naquadah Hyper Reactor (UEV, GTNA original) burns the same fuels at four times the EU per mB and can be boosted with plasma.

Large Naquadah Reactor Naquadah Hyper Reactor Tier UHV UEV Size 25 × 25 × 9 96 × 38 × 24 Output Dynamo or Laser Source Hatch (one) Dynamo or Laser Source Hatch (one) Hatches up to 3 Input Hatches, 1 Maintenance up to 3 Input Hatches, 1 Maintenance Controller Assembly Line, research on the UV Field Generator Assembly Line (4 Large Naquadah Reactors), research on the Large Naquadah Reactor Blocks catalog page catalog page

docs.title: Fuels
docs.text:
Both fuels are made in the Large Chemical Reactor at UV (4000 ticks, 20,000 mB each):

  • Naquadah Fuel: 16 Naquadah dust, 30,000 mB hydrogen, 15,000 mB nitrogen, 8,000 mB fluorine, 8,000 mB nitric acid.
  • Enriched Naquadah Fuel: 16 Enriched Naquadah dust, 4 antimony dust, 48,000 mB hydrogen, 30,000 mB nitrogen, 12,000 mB fluorine, 8,000 mB xenon, 6,000 mB radon.

A modpack can replace these recipes by id.

docs.title: Energy per mB
docs.text:
\[ \frac{\text{EU}}{\text{mB}} = \frac{t \cdot V}{\text{fuel (mB)}} \] Machine Recipe Fuel per run Time EU/t EU per mB of fuel Large Naquadah Fuel + 80 mB hydrogen 16 mB 875 ticks \(2^{21}\) (UHV) 114,688,000 Large Enriched Naquadah Fuel + 80 mB hydrogen 16 mB 1,250 ticks \(2^{21}\) (UHV) 163,840,000 Large Naquadah Fuel + 40 mB oxygen plasma 160 mB 28,000 ticks \(2^{19}\) (UV) 91,750,400 Large Enriched Naquadah Fuel + 40 mB nitrogen plasma 160 mB 40,000 ticks \(2^{19}\) (UV) 131,072,000 Hyper Naquadah Fuel + 80 mB hydrogen 16 mB 875 ticks \(2^{23}\) (UEV) 458,752,000 Hyper Enriched Naquadah Fuel + 80 mB hydrogen 16 mB 1,250 ticks \(2^{23}\) (UEV) 655,360,000

On the Large reactor the plasma recipes trade some EU per mB for a run 32 times longer at UV.

docs.title: Hyper Reactor boost
docs.text:
When a booster plasma is in an input hatch at the start of a run, the run is multiplied by the booster's parallel: fuel, hydrogen and EU/t all grow together, and the booster is consumed once per run. The best booster present wins.

\[ \text{EU/t} = 2^{23} \cdot p \qquad \text{fuel per run} = 16\,p\ \text{mB} \qquad p \le \text{booster parallel} \] Booster (per run) Parallel \(p\) EU/t with naquadah fuel none 1 \(2^{23}\) = 8,388,608 40 mB oxygen plasma 8 \(2^{26}\) = 67,108,864 40 mB nitrogen plasma 16 \(2^{27}\) = 134,217,728

The parallel is limited by the fuel in the hatches, never by energy. The EU per mB of fuel stays the same, so boosting raises power, not efficiency.

docs.title: Original multiblocks
docs.text:
Machines designed for GTNA, with no equivalent in another mod. Each controller has its own screen with a field manual (in English, Portuguese and Chinese), and each page below has the formulas, tables computed from the code and the current screens.

Machine Tier What it does Only it makes Kinetic Orbital Lance UEV fires projectiles at moons and asteroids from a capacitor bank and recovers the fragments in capsules Primordial Tholin (Arrokoth), Nexium (Nexus-1) Dimensional Rift Gate UIV opens rifts to seeded dimensions; tune frequency, phase and amplitude until the rift holds one exclusive material per biome: Prismatium, Chronomercury, Forgecore, Vivispore, Abyssal Antimatter, Precursor Residue, Void Ash Antimatter Collider Ring UIV collides counter-rotating beams for exotic particles and stores antiprotons in Penning traps antiproton cells, Higgs and top particles Stellar Containment Chamber MAX holds a neutron star in field bands and sends the energy of its spin to the Nexus network Magnetar Crystals, Degenerate Core Matter

The four feed each other and the endgame: their products go into the Forge of the Gods, the Eye of Harmony field generators and the antimatter fuel rods.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• Lance → Nexium → Collider (tier-4 dipoles) and Magnetarium (the slug that breaks Nexus-1).
  • Rift Gate → Forgecore plates → Stellar Chamber (holds the magnetar field).
  • Stellar Chamber → Magnetar Crystal → Magnetarium → Lance.
  • Collider → X-Nexus → Rift Gate (anchors past depth 40) and the Forge of the Gods.

docs.title: Coming next
docs.text: The Pressurized Water Reactor (IV) is designed; planned page.

docs.title: Steam age
docs.text: GTNA turns the steam age into a full factory tier: large steam multiblocks with parallel, steam without pipes, machines that need no energy at all, and a steam elevator that reaches other planets. Every machine here has a catalog page with its structure.

docs.title: Steam supply
docs.text:
Machine What it gives Large Steam Solar Boiler expandable field of solar boiling cells, up to 63 blocks sideways and 125 back; output grows with sunlit cells. The only structure that takes the wireless steam output hatch Cactus Wonder burns coal and charcoal (8,000 mB of steam each) or coal blocks (90,000 mB), one item per second; needs fully grown cacti on its sand floor Large Steam Storage Tank stores 120,000,000 mB of steam to smooth out boiler output Dimensionally Transcendent Steam Boiler a very large late boiler from GregTech Leisure

Then carry the steam with the wireless steam network instead of pipes.

docs.title: Large steam machines
docs.text:
Steam versions of the basic GregTech machines, ported from GT: Not Leisure: furnace, macerator, alloy smelter, compressor, extractor, forge hammer, lathe, cutter, bender, extruder, wiremill, forming press, sifter, mixer, centrifuge, thermal centrifuge, ore washer, chemical bath and circuit assembler.

  • They run many items at once. The parallel cap depends on the machine and can be lowered in the controller:

    Parallel Machines 128 Furnace, Crusher 96 Ore Washer 64 Alloy Smelter, Hammer, Mixer, Centrifuge, Thermal Centrifuge, Bath 48 Compressor, Extractor 32 Forming Press 16 Lathe, Cutting Machine, Bending Machine, Extruder, Wiremill, Sifter 4 Circuit Assembler

  • Each is faster than its single-block version: 10× for the Furnace, 5× for the Ore Washer, 2.5× for the Compressor and Forming Press, about 1.75× for the Alloy Smelter and Extractor, 2× for the rest.

  • High pressure: build the structure with the steel casings instead of the bronze ones (every casing must be steel) and the machine runs 2× faster for 2× steam.
  • Use Huge Steam Buses (54 slots) to feed them.

Their recipes use GTNA's hydraulic components, made by hand or in the Steam Manufacturer.

docs.title: Primitive machines
docs.text:
None of these uses EU. Only the Infernal Coke Oven uses steam.

Machine Highlights Infernal Coke Oven speeds up by 1% every 5 s up to 10×, and gains 16 parallel every 10 minutes (8 up to 256). Uses steam: 6,400 L/s plus 1,600 L/s per stage. The speed bonus decays while idle Hyper Pressure Reactor fluid reactions with no energy and no steam, 1 parallel; the Compact version has 512 Leap Forward One Blast Furnace primitive blast furnace that grows: every extra layer doubles the parallel (up to 32,000) and adds 20 s to the 20 s cycle Primitive Stone Furnace smelts every furnace recipe at once, each in 1 tick Brick Kiln fires bricks and ceramics from compressed clay and coal

docs.title: Specialists
docs.text:
Machine What it does Stone SuperHeater super-heating recipes of the steam age, 32 parallel Steam Woodcutter sapling in, logs out, 64 parallel Steam Cobbler rock breaker; the circuit picks the stone, 16 parallel Steam Manufacturer Hydraulic Manufacturing, 16 parallel; builds the biggest steam machines Steam Supercompressor 256 parallel; made from 64 Large Steam Compressors Void Miner SteamGate Aged mines raw ores from nothing; see void mining

Most of them let you lower the parallel in the controller.

docs.title: Steam Elevator
docs.text:
The Steam Elevator is a modular structure with up to 12 module slots. With Ad Astra installed, Set out opens the planet selection. Its modules only work while attached:

Module Tiers Flight, Beacon, Weather, Monster Repellator, Entity Crusher, Oil Drill I, II, III Greenhouse Planting, Steam-Powered Apiary, Bee Breeding, Ore Processing one each

The Bee Breeding module exists only when Productive Bees is installed.

docs.title: Balance for modpacks
docs.text: A modpack can scale the parallel and the duration of every GTNA steam multiblock from one place in Java (GTNASteamBalance), for example per difficulty.

docs.title: Antimatter Collider Ring
docs.text:
Accelerates two counter-rotating beams around a 3 km ring and collides them. Production runs make exotic particles and antiprotons; physics runs gather luminosity to discover particles and complete committee proposals.

Tier UIV Size 155 × 127 × 137 Energy owner's Nexus network (magnets and traps) Fluid liquid helium Controller Assembly Line (UIV), research on the UIV Emitter Blocks catalog page

docs.title: Structure and hatches
docs.text:
Hatch Max Use Input Hatch 4 liquid helium Input Bus 2 fine Nexium wire (Neutronium Magnet proposal) Output Bus 4 particles, Antiproton Penning Cells Collision Detector Hatch 1 needed to record physics runs Beam Dump 1 halves the quench recovery

While running, the ring and gyro blocks are taken into the controller and drawn moving; they come back when the machine stops.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Click the mode line to switch. Production: particles with 10% yield before evidence, 40% at 3σ and 100% after the 5σ discovery; antiprotons fill the traps and leave as Antiproton Penning Cells (1e11 each).

Physics: the integrated luminosity raises each particle's significance and advances the active proposal.

\[ \begin{aligned} E_{\text{beam}} &= 0.3\,B\,\rho \quad (\text{GeV, } B \text{ in T, } \rho = 3000\ \text{m}) \\ E_{\text{cm}} &= 2\left(150 + (E_{\text{beam}} - 150) \cdot \min\!\left(1, \tfrac{t}{20\ \text{s}}\right)\right)\ \text{GeV} \\ \mathcal{L} &= \frac{f_{\text{rev}}\,n_b\,N^{2}}{4\pi\sigma^{2}}, \qquad f_{\text{rev}} = \frac{c}{2\pi\rho} \approx 15{,}905\ \text{Hz},\ N = 10^{11} \\ \Delta\!\int\!\mathcal{L} &= \mathcal{L} \cdot 10^{-39} \cdot 10^{5}\ \text{fb}^{-1}\ \text{per second} \\ Z &= s\,\sqrt{\textstyle\int\!\mathcal{L}} \cdot (\sqrt{2}\ \text{with the vertex detector}) \end{aligned} \]

A full ring ramps in 20 s from 150 GeV. Base luminosity is \(3.16 \times 10^{32}\) cm⁻²s⁻¹ (0.03 fb⁻¹/s); with stochastic cooling and the vertex detector it is \(4.94 \times 10^{33}\) (0.49 fb⁻¹/s). Production yield: 10% before 3σ, 40% from 3σ, 100% from 5σ.

Magnet B (T) Max beam (TeV) Upkeep (EU/t) Liquid helium (L/s) Quench pause NbTi 8.3 7.47 \(2^{33}\) 0.5 (0.3) 60 s Nb₃Sn 12 10.8 \(2^{34}\) 1 (0.6) 120 s REBCO 20 18 \(2^{35}\) 2 (1.2) 180 s Neutronium 45 40.5 \(2^{36}\) 4 (2.4) 240 s Infinity 120 108 \(2^{37}\) 8 (4.8) 300 s

Helium in brackets: after the cryogenic Penning proposal. The quench pause doubles without a Beam Dump.

Particle Threshold E_cm (GeV) \(s\) fb⁻¹ for 5σ with vertex hours at base luminosity Antiprotons 5.6 50 0.01 \(5.00 \times 10^{-3}\) \(8.78 \times 10^{-5}\) Kaons 1 30 0.03 0.01 \(2.44 \times 10^{-4}\) Lambda 2.5 8 0.39 0.2 \(3.43 \times 10^{-3}\) Charm 10 4 1.56 0.78 0.01 Bottom 40 1.5 11.11 5.56 0.1 W boson 161 0.6 69.44 34.72 0.61 Z boson 182 0.8 39.06 19.53 0.34 Higgs 250 0.08 3,906 1,953 34.29 Top 346 0.15 1,111 555.56 9.75 X(Nexus) 4,800 0.02 62,500 31,250 548.68

X-Nexus also needs the heavy-ion proposal.

docs.title: Power and cooling
docs.text:
\[ \begin{aligned} P_{\text{magnets}} &= 2^{\,33 + k_{\text{magnet}}}\ \text{EU/t} \qquad P_{\text{traps}} = 2^{\,20 + k_{\text{trap}}}\ \text{EU/t} \\ \dot V_{\text{He}} &= 0.5 \cdot 2^{k_{\text{magnet}}}\ \text{L/s} \quad (\times 0.6\ \text{after cryogenic Penning}) \\ \text{trap capacity} &= 10^{12} \cdot 4^{\,k_{\text{trap}} - 1}\ \bar p \end{aligned} \]

Less helium than the demand quenches the magnets: the beam stops for 60·(tier + 1) seconds.

docs.title: Committee proposals
docs.text:
The committee grants one proposal at a time, in this order. Physics runs advance the active proposal.

# Proposal Needs Gives 1 Nb3Sn magnet test 5 fb⁻¹ delivered magnet Nb₃Sn (12 T) 2 Vertex detector charm at 5σ significance × √2, beam 16 µm 3 Stochastic cooling 20 fb⁻¹ 1,000 bunches 4 Cryogenic Penning 10¹³ antiprotons stored or 40 fb⁻¹ trap tier 3, helium × 0.6 5 REBCO magnet W and Z at 5σ magnet REBCO (20 T) 6 e+e- collisions bottom at 5σ e+e− button (electron beams) 7 Heavy ions top at 5σ heavy ions: X-Nexus can be produced 8 Neutronium magnet Higgs at 5σ + 1024 fine Nexium wire magnet Neutronium (45 T) 9 Beyond the Standard Model X-Nexus at 3σ magnet Infinity (120 T)

If the trap upkeep is not paid the stored antiprotons annihilate and damage the ring. Side tabs: Standard Model board and Committee.

Electron beams. After the e+e− proposal the e+e− button switches the ring to electron beams. Synchrotron light caps them at 100 GeV per beam (like LEP): \(E_{\text{cm}} \le 200\) GeV, so W, Z, charm and bottom are reachable but not the Higgs or the top. Clean collisions count twice in physics runs. Switch back to protons for the heavier particles.

docs.title: Endgame
docs.text:
Exclusive: antiproton cells go into the Cosmic Neutronium and Infinity fuel rods and the Forge of Gods siphon. Higgs and top: Gravitational Lens. X-Nexus: Forge of Gods controller and deep anchors.

Needs: the Neutronium Magnet proposal only closes with 1024 fine Nexium wire in the input buses; the wire is wound into the tier-4 dipoles when it closes.

Nexium comes from the Kinetic Orbital Lance (Nexus-1); the Rift Gate needs your X-Nexus to go past depth 40.

docs.text:
Opens a rift to a seeded dimension and pulls resources from it. Tune frequency, phase and amplitude towards the seed's hidden optimum to raise the resonance.

docs.title: Structure and hatches
docs.text: Hatch Max Use Input Hatch 4 SpaceTime Input Bus 4 Rift Probes, Depth Anchors, Contained X-Nexus Output Bus 4 biome dusts, Rift Singularity Rift Tuning Hatch 1 redstone 0–15 sets the amplitude to 0–100%

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
Click Open for a rift with a random seed. Tune with [--] [-] [+] [++] (±10 / ±1). Each Rift Probe consumed narrows the tolerances by 20%.

\[ \begin{aligned} R &= \exp\!\left(-\left(\frac{f - f^{*}}{\sigma_f}\right)^{2} - \left(\frac{\Delta\varphi}{\sigma_\varphi}\right)^{2} - \left(\frac{A - A^{*}}{\sigma_A}\right)^{2}\right) \\ \sigma_f &= 260\ \text{THz} \cdot 0.8^{n} \qquad \sigma_\varphi = 100^\circ \cdot 0.8^{n} \qquad \sigma_A = 45\,\% \cdot 0.8^{n} \end{aligned} \]

\(f\) goes from 1 to 1000 THz, \(\varphi\) from 0 to 360° and \(A\) from 0 to 100%; \((f^*, \varphi^*, A^*)\) is the seed's hidden optimum and \(n\) the number of probes consumed on this seed. Each knob shows a hot/cold bar for its own axis.

Probes \(\sigma_f\) (THz) \(\sigma_\varphi\) (°) \(\sigma_A\) (%) Window for R ≥ 0.9 in f 0 260 100 45 ±84.39 THz 2 166.4 64 28.8 ±54.01 THz 4 106.5 40.96 18.43 ±34.57 THz 6 68.16 26.21 11.8 ±22.12 THz 8 43.62 16.78 7.55 ±14.16 THz 10 27.92 10.74 4.83 ±9.06 THz

docs.title: Power and stability
docs.text:
Field = 2^36 EU/t from the Nexus network while open; without it the rift collapses

SpaceTime fluid keeps it stable: each litre adds 2 stability. Losses grow with low resonance and with depth.

\[ \begin{aligned} \frac{dS}{dt} &= 2\,\dot V - \lambda\,(1 - R)\left(1 + \frac{D}{10}\right) - 0.4\,(8 - P) \\ \lambda &= 1.5\,(1.3 - C) \\ \dot V_{\text{SpaceTime}} &= 16 \cdot \frac{\lambda\,(1 - R)\,(1 + D/10) + 0.4\,(8 - P)}{2}\ \text{L/s} \end{aligned} \]

\(S\) is the stability (0–100), \(D\) the depth, \(P\) the active pylons (4 in the current structure) and \(C\) the chord consonance (next section). The machine drains enough SpaceTime each second to cover the upkeep plus one unit; each litre of SpaceTime is worth 1/16 of a stability unit.

R D SpaceTime (L/s), no chord, 4 pylons 0.5 1 19.4 0.9 1 14.12 0.9 5 14.6 0.98 5 13.16 0.98 8 13.23 1 8 12.8

docs.title: Harmonics
docs.text:
Holding R ≥ 0.9 for 30 s records the seed's harmonic. Click recorded harmonics to load up to 5 in the chord: consonant chords (octave, fifth) are stable; dissonant chords (tritone, minor second) dig deeper but cost more SpaceTime. Each recorded harmonic raises the maximum depth by 5 (base 5).

Holding R ≥ 0.98 for a minute can give a Rift Singularity. Stability at 0 collapses the rift; R under 0.2 for 10 s inverts it (−10 stability). Side tabs: Seismograph and Atlas.

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{c}(p\!:\!q) &= \frac{1}{\log_2 (p\,q)} \qquad C = \overline{\text{c}} \ (\text{mean of the chord; 0.3 with no chord}) \\ D_{\max} &= \left\lfloor (5 + 5\,h) \cdot \max\!\left(0.5,\ 1 + 3\,(0.3 - C)\right) \right\rfloor \end{aligned} \]

\(h\) is the number of recorded harmonics. The table uses the five harmonics of the surface biomes (\(h = 5\), base 30).

Interval Ratio Consonance λ factor (alone) Max depth (alone) Recorded in Octave 2:1 1 0.3 15 not dropped by any biome Fifth 3:2 0.39 0.91 22 Crystal plains Fourth 4:3 0.28 1.02 31 Spore forest Major third 5:4 0.23 1.07 36 Mercury ocean Minor sixth 8:5 0.19 1.11 40 Forge world Minor seventh 9:5 0.18 1.12 40 Civilisation relic Tritone 45:32 0.1 1.2 48 Antimatter abyss Minor second 16:15 0.13 1.17 45 Void

docs.title: Endgame
docs.text:
Each biome drops dusts of its materials into the output buses. Rate of each material:

\[ \text{dusts/s} = 16 \cdot R^{2} \cdot D^{1.5} \cdot \frac{S}{100} \] Biome Chance Min. depth Dusts Crystal plains 30% — Prismatium, Certus Quartz, Silicon, Titanium Mercury ocean 20% — Chronomercury, Gold, Thallium, Cinnabar Forge world 15% — Forgecore, Tungsten, Osmium, Iridium Spore forest 15% — Vivispore, Wood, Carbon, Phosphorus Antimatter abyss 8% — Abyssal Antimatter, Naquadah, Naquadah Enriched Civilisation relic 7% 20 Precursor Residue, Naquadria, Trinium, Duranium Void 5% 40 Void Ash, Neutronium, Space Time

Exclusive: one material per biome (Prismatium, Chronomercury, Forgecore, Vivispore, Abyssal Antimatter, Precursor Residue, Void Ash). The Singularity goes into the Forge of Gods controller and Advanced+ Eye of Harmony fields.

Needs: from depth 40 on, each Depth Anchor also takes one Contained X-Nexus; without one it stays in the bus.

X-Nexus comes from the Antimatter Collider Ring; the Stellar Chamber needs your Forgecore to hold a magnetar.

Known issues

Report anything else on the issue tracker.
