docs.title: Kinetic Orbital Lance
docs.text:
Fires projectiles from a capacitor bank at moons and asteroids and recovers the fragments in return capsules, which land as dusts of the body's materials.

Tier UEV Size 242 × 130 × 142 Energy owner's Nexus network, up to \(2^{36}\) EU/t into the bank Computation up to \(2^{20}\) CWU/t (aim) Controller Assembly Line (UEV), research on the UEV Electric Piston Blocks catalog page

docs.title: Structure and hatches
docs.text:
Hatch Max Use Input Bus 4 projectile ingots Output Bus 4 dusts from the capsules Computation Data Reception Hatch 1 aim (without it the aim is blind) Barrel Liner Hatch 1 spare liners, swapped in automatically Target Cartridge Hatch 1 up to 8 target cartridges, one per shot in turn

While formed, the gun (everything above the turret ring) is taken into the controller and drawn slewing to the target.

docs.title: Bank and firing
docs.text:
The bank charges from the Nexus network at up to \(2^{36}\) EU/t. With auto-fire on, the Lance fires the whole bank as soon as it is full, the target can be aimed at and an input bus holds a projectile that can break that body.

\[ \begin{aligned} E &= 4 \times 10^{12}\ \text{EU} \\ \eta &= \min\!\left(0.85,\ 0.35 + \textstyle\sum \Delta\eta_{\text{rail}} \cdot \left(1 - 0.5\,\tfrac{n_{\text{rail}}}{8}\right)\right) \\ M_{\text{frag}} &= \frac{0.2\,\eta\,E \cdot 1000\ \text{J/EU}}{H} \\ M_{\text{rec}} &= M_{\text{frag}} \cdot r \cdot A \end{aligned} \]

\(H\) is the body hardness (J/kg), \(r\) the capsule recovery (0.6 without a capsule component) and \(A\) the accuracy (next section). The capsule lands after \(t = 30\ \text{s} \cdot \ln(1 + d / 50\ \text{Mm})\) and unloads one dust per 100 t, split evenly over the body's materials. A capsule that does not fit waits in the queue.

Projectiles are ingots. The type only decides which body can be hit: Nexus-1 only breaks under Magnetarium, every projectile works on the other bodies.

Projectile (ingot) Mass (kg) Breaks Nexus-1 Naquadah Alloy 50 — Trinium 80 — Neutronium 400 — Cosmic Neutronium 800 — White Dwarf Matter 1,200 — Magnetarium 2,000 ✅

docs.title: Targets and aim
docs.text:
Start with the Moon. A body becomes targetable once its parents are surveyed to 100% (recover their characteristic mass). Cartridges in the Target Cartridge Hatch pick the target and take turns shot by shot.

The reception hatch must be linked by optical cable to a transmission hatch of a working computation network (e.g. Network Switch fed by a Supercomputer). More CWU/t tightens the aim; it matters for far bodies.

\[ \begin{aligned} S &= 1 - e^{-M / M_{\text{car}}} && \text{survey, 99\% counts as complete} \\ \theta &= \frac{10^{-9}\,u}{\sqrt{\text{CWU/t} / 1000}} + 2 \times 10^{-10} \cdot \frac{\max(0,\ T - 300)}{100} \\ A &= \max\!\left(0,\ 1 - \frac{d\,\theta}{5000\ \text{m}}\right) \end{aligned} \]

\(M\) is the mass recovered from the body, \(u\) the aim factor of the sensor (1 without one), \(T\) the barrel temperature (K) and \(d\) the distance. The Lance asks the computation hatch for up to \(2^{20}\) (1,048,576) CWU/t; a bigger network aims better.

* No bench components (\(\eta = 0.35\), \(r = 0.6\), \(u = 1\)), \(2^{20}\) CWU/t, cold barrel.

docs.title: Barrel bench and wear
docs.text:
Click components on the bench line or in the Bench tab. Up to 8 rails (shift-click removes one); every other slot takes one component. Surveying a body to 100% unlocks the components that come from it. The loadout must fit three budgets, otherwise the Lance does not fire:

\[ \sum m \le 800\ \text{t} \qquad \sum Q \le 60 \qquad \frac{n_{\text{rail}}}{8} \le 1 \] Component Slot Effect Mass (t) Heat Unlocked by rail_cu_nb Rail \(\Delta\eta = +0.02\) 40 3 start rail_superconductor Rail \(\Delta\eta = +0.04\) 60 1 Phobos rail_graphene Rail \(\Delta\eta = +0.07\) 140 2 Psyche cooling_helium Cooling \(C_{\text{barrel}} \times 2\) 30 -10 Ceres cooling_superconductor Cooling \(C_{\text{barrel}} \times 4\) 60 -25 Europa cooling_plasma_ice Cooling \(C_{\text{barrel}} \times 8\) 90 -60 Arrokoth sensor_telescope Sensor \(u = 0.7\) 10 2 Moon sensor_interferometer Sensor \(u = 0.35\) 40 2 Europa sensor_lens Sensor \(u = 0.17\) 80 2 Arrokoth capsule_ablative Capsule \(r = 0.75\) 0 0 Ceres capsule_magnetic Capsule \(r = 0.85\) 0 0 Psyche capsule_fold Capsule \(r = 0.95\) 0 0 Nexus-1 salvo_splitter Salvo 2 projectiles per shot 50 5 Vesta \[ \begin{aligned} \Delta T &= \frac{(1 - \eta)\,E}{C_{\text{barrel}}}, \qquad C_{\text{barrel}} = 2 \times 10^{9}\ \text{EU/K} \times k_{\text{cooling}} \\ \dot T_{\text{cooling}} &= -\frac{2^{34} \cdot 20\ \text{EU/s}}{C_{\text{barrel}}} \quad (\text{down to 300 K}) \\ W &\mathrel{+}= \frac{E}{E_{\text{liner}}} \end{aligned} \]

Each shot wears the liner and heats the barrel. A worn liner (100%) or a barrel over 2500 K misfires. Spare liners (naquadah alloy or neutronium plates) in the Barrel Liner Hatch are swapped in automatically. Side tabs: Orbital map and Bench.

Liner (plate or dense plate) \(E_{liner}\) (EU) Full shots Naquadah Alloy \(5.00 \times 10^{13}\) 12.5 Neutronium \(2.00 \times 10^{14}\) 50

Without bench components a full shot heats the barrel by 1,300 K and the base cooling removes about 172 K per second.

docs.title: Endgame
docs.text:
Exclusive: capsules from Arrokoth bring Primordial Tholin (Forge of Gods structure casing); capsules from Nexus-1 bring Nexium (Collider dipoles, Magnetarium).

Needs: Nexus-1's crust only breaks under Magnetarium ingots (Magnetar Slug, 2000 t). Mixer: 2 Nexium + 1 Magnetar Crystal + 4 White Dwarf Matter dust, then the blast furnace at 12000 K.

The Magnetar Crystal comes from the Stellar Containment Chamber; the Collider needs your Nexium for its last magnets.

Known issues

  • The projectile mass, the impact regime and the salvo splitter do not change what comes back yet: the recovered mass depends only on \(\eta\), \(E\), \(H\), \(r\) and \(A\).
  • The bank has one capacitor ring (\(4 \times 10^{12}\) EU); extra rings are not in the game yet, so the mass budget is 800 t and the heat budget 60.

Report anything else on the issue tracker.

docs.title: Stellar Containment Chamber
docs.text:
Holds a neutron star in containment bands and turns its spin into EU for the owner's Nexus wireless network. There are no recipes: the star has a mass, a spin period and a crust, and everything you do changes them.

Tier MAX Size 93 × 93 × 93 Energy produces EU into the owner's Nexus network Output up to \(2^{59}\) EU/t (neutron star), \(2^{62}\) EU/t (black hole) Controller Assembly Line (UXV), research on the UXV Field Generator Blocks catalog page

docs.title: Structure and hatches
docs.text:
Hatch Max Use Input Hatch 8 star matter (any fluid form) Output Bus 4 neutronium, white dwarf matter, crystals, core matter Mass Injector 4 dusts and ingots of star matter; Forgecore plates Seismic Probe 1 decodes starquakes

The Degenerate Matter Core (radius 7) at the centre must be complete. When the bands get power the core is taken into the star; it comes back as blocks when the chamber stops or the structure breaks.

docs.title: Power and extraction
docs.text:
The bands draw their upkeep from the owner's Nexus network every second. Without it the star stays dark, and a lit star takes containment damage.

Set the extraction with [-] and [+] as 2^n EU/t (n from 40 to 62). The energy goes to the Nexus network.

\[ \begin{aligned} I &= 0.4\,M R^{2}, \quad R = 12\ \text{km} \qquad E_{\text{rot}} = \tfrac12 I\,\omega^{2} \cdot 10^{-20}\ \text{EU/J}, \quad \omega = \frac{2\pi}{P} \\ P_{\text{dipole}} &= \frac{B^{2} R^{6} \omega^{4}}{6 c^{3}} \cdot 10^{-20}\ \text{EU/J}, \quad B = 6.7 \times 10^{11}\ \text{T}\ (\times 4\ \text{magnetar}) \\ \text{upkeep} &= 2^{\,40 + 2k}\ \text{EU/t} \qquad \text{cap} = 2^{\,55 + k}\ \text{EU/t}\ (\tfrac12\ \text{until the millisecond region}) \end{aligned} \] Band tier Unlocked by Upkeep (EU/t) Cap (EU/t) Quake capacity 1 start \(2^{42}\) \(2^{56}\) \(1.00 \times 10^{16}\) 2 micro quake decoded \(2^{44}\) \(2^{57}\) \(1.00 \times 10^{17}\) 3 Vela quake decoded \(2^{46}\) \(2^{58}\) \(1.00 \times 10^{18}\) 4 Vela + record spin (< 1.4 ms) \(2^{48}\) \(2^{59}\) \(1.00 \times 10^{19}\)

Extraction also mines the crust: \(\text{EU/t} / 2^{52}\) neutronium dusts per second.

docs.title: Feeding and outputs
docs.text:
Feed star matter through Input Hatches (liquid, molten, gas or plasma) or as dusts and ingots through a Mass Injector (144 mB each). Feeding adds mass and spins the star up, like a recycled pulsar; 15% of the mass leaves as binding energy, paid at once as EU.

Outputs in the Output Buses: neutronium dust from crust mining (grows with extraction) and white dwarf matter dust from starquakes.

\[ \begin{aligned} \Delta J &= \Delta M\,\sqrt{G M R} \qquad \omega' = \frac{I\omega + \Delta J}{I'} \\ M' &= M + 0.85\,\Delta M \qquad E_{\text{bind}} = 0.15\,\Delta M\,c^{2} \cdot 10^{-26}\ \text{EU/J} \end{aligned} \] Feed M☉ per mB M☉ per dust or ingot Magnetohydrodynamically Constrained Star Matter \(1.00 \times 10^{-7}\) \(1.44 \times 10^{-5}\) White Dwarf Matter \(1.00 \times 10^{-8}\) \(1.44 \times 10^{-6}\) Raw Star Matter \(1.00 \times 10^{-9}\) \(1.44 \times 10^{-7}\) Neutronium \(1.00 \times 10^{-10}\) \(1.44 \times 10^{-8}\)

docs.title: Starquakes and bands
docs.text:
Changing the spin builds stress; at 1 a starquake happens. Only a Seismic Probe decodes quakes (Seismogram tab). Decoded quakes raise the band tier: micro → tier 2, Vela (fast feeding) → tier 3, Vela plus a record spin (< 1.4 ms) → tier 4.

The Magnetar button inverts the band field. After 10 minutes the star becomes a magnetar and can give antiquakes.

A quake bigger than the band capacity, or any quake with unpowered bands, damages containment by 10%. At 100% the star loses 10% of its mass.

\[ \sigma \mathrel{+}= 10^{4} \cdot \frac{|\Delta\omega|}{\omega} \quad (\text{a quake at σ ≥ 1}) \] Quake How ΔΩ/Ω Micro steady extraction \(5.00 \times 10^{-9}\) Crab vary the extraction \(5.00 \times 10^{-8}\) Vela fast feeding \(1.10 \times 10^{-6}\) Anti magnetar only \(-3.00 \times 10^{-7}\) Collapse cross the TOV edge \(1.00 \times 10^{-4}\)

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Above the TOV limit (2.2 M☉) the star collapses into a black hole, for good. Energy then comes from the ergosphere: the faster it spun when it collapsed, the more there is.

\[ \begin{aligned} P_{\text{Kepler}} &= 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R^{3}}{G M}} \\ a^{*} &= \min\!\left(0.998,\ \frac{J c}{G M^{2}}\right) \qquad E_{\text{hole}} = \left(1 - \sqrt{\frac{1 + \sqrt{1 - a^{*2}}}{2}}\right) M c^{2} \end{aligned} \] Mass (M☉) Kepler period (ms) 1.2 0.65 1.4 0.61 1.8 0.53 2.1 0.49 2.2 0.48 \(a^*\) Extractable share of \(Mc^2\) 0.3 1.16% 0.6 5.13% 0.9 15.27% 1 27.09%

The TOV limit is 2.2 M☉, or 2.4 M☉ after an anti-quake has been decoded. Mass–period regions: young (< 30 ms), millisecond (< 10 ms after feeding), record (< 1.4 ms), magnetar (600 s of inverted field), TOV edge (> 2.1 M☉), black hole.

docs.title: Endgame
docs.text:
Exclusive: a magnetar starquake (field inverted for 600 s) leaves 4 Magnetar Crystals; a collapse leaves 64 Degenerate Core Matter (Eye of Harmony fields from Advanced tier).

Needs: the inverted field tears the crust. Each 60 s of magnetar field takes one Forgecore plate from the Mass Injector; without one the field drops and the crust takes 10% damage.

Forgecore comes from the Forge World biome of the Dimensional Rift Gate; the Lance needs your crystals for the Magnetar Slug.

docs.title: Hatches and parts
docs.text: GTNA's multiblock parts. Each one works only in structures that accept it: in JEI/EMI, hover a hatch position of the structure preview to see which parts fit there.

docs.title: Speed and parallel
docs.text:
Part Tiers What it does Accelerate Hatch LV–MAX shortens every recipe, on top of the normal overclock Overclock Hatch UV–MAX makes each overclock step cut more time Thread Hatch ZPM–MAX runs different recipes at the same time Parallel Control Hatch (UHV+) UHV–OpV 1,024 to 262,144 parallel

The three adjustable hatches have a small UI: open them to lower their effect when a recipe should run slower.

docs.title: Steam
docs.text: Part What it does Wireless Steam Input / Output Hatch steam without pipes, see the wireless steam network Huge Steam Input / Output Bus steam item buses with 54 slots

docs.title: AE2 and energy
docs.text: Pattern Buffers, the Pattern Buffer Proxy, the ME Export Buffer and the storage access hatches are on the ME Pattern Buffers page. Wireless energy and dynamo hatches are on the Nexus energy network page.

docs.title: Restricted parts
docs.text:
These parts break normal balance. They exist for creative building, testing and packs that want them:

Part Tiers What it does Infinite Input Bus / Hatch LV–MAX compatible multiblocks read the items or fluids inside without consuming them Output Boost Hatch, Item Bus and Fluid Hatch LV–MAX multiply recipe outputs: 25× up to MV, then 50×, 100×, 250×… up to 250,000× at MAX Infinite Steam Input Bus — the steam version of the Infinite Input Bus Output Boost Steam Output Bus — multiplies a steam multiblock's item outputs

Each group can be turned off, hidden from JEI or stripped of its recipes in config/gtna/balance/restricted_items.json; see Configuration. Creative-only debug parts, without recipes, also exist for testing.

docs.title: Accelerate Hatch
docs.text:
Shortens every recipe of the multiblock, on top of the normal overclock. Ported from GregTech Odyssey.

Tiers LV to MAX Fits electric multiblocks (GTCEu and GTNA) whose structure accepts it, and the auxiliary modules that add it Per machine one

docs.title: Duration
docs.text:
The value is the duration left, in percent of the original:

Hatch Duration Hatch Duration LV 50% UV 36% MV 48% UHV 34% HV 46% UEV 32% EV 44% UIV 30% IV 42% UXV 28% LuV 40% OpV 26% ZPM 38% MAX 24%

The formula is \(50 - 2 \cdot (\text{tier} - 1)\) percent. You can raise the value in the hatch UI, up to 100% (no effect).

docs.title: Penalty
docs.text:
For each tier the recipe is above the hatch, add 20 points. A low-tier recipe in a high-tier machine is never penalised.

Example

An HV hatch (46%) running an EV recipe: 46% + 20% = 66%. A 100-tick recipe takes 66 ticks.

The final value stays between 1% and 100%. Values are in config/gtna/balance/hatches.json (accelerateHatch), and the EU cost multiplier is machines.accelerateHatchEnergyCost in config/gtna.yaml (default 1.5).

docs.title: With other hatches
docs.text: Everything multiplies: \(\text{duration} = \text{base} \times \text{overclock steps} \times \text{accelerate}\). See the Overclock Hatch for an example.

docs.title: Parallel Control Hatch (UHV+)
docs.text:
GTCEu's Parallel Control Hatches stop at 256 parallel (UV). GTNA continues the line with the same name:

Hatch Max parallel UHV 1,024 UEV 4,096 UIV 16,384 UXV 65,536 OpV 262,144

They use GTCEu's normal Parallel Hatch slot, so they fit every multiblock that takes a Parallel Hatch, one per machine. With a Thread Hatch, the parallel is split between the threads.

docs.title: Huge Steam Buses
docs.text:
Steam item buses with 54 slots, for steam multiblocks that process many stacks at once, such as the Large Steam machines.

Bus Slots Huge Steam Input Bus 54 Huge Steam Output Bus 54

They go wherever a steam item bus goes. Two related parts:

  • Infinite Steam Input Bus: steam multiblocks read its items without consuming them (a restricted part, see Hatches and parts).
  • Output Boost Steam Output Bus: multiplies the item outputs of a steam multiblock (also restricted).

docs.title: Overclock Hatch
docs.text:
Improves the overclock curve itself. Normally each overclock step (4× EU/t) halves the duration; with this hatch each step divides it by the hatch's divisor. Ported from GregTech Odyssey.

Hatch Divisor per step Duration per step UV 2 50% UHV 3 33.3% UEV 4 25% UIV 5 20% UXV 6 16.7% OpV 7 14.3% MAX 8 12.5%

The UV hatch equals the standard overclock, so the gain starts at UHV. You can lower the divisor in the hatch UI. Values are in config/gtna/balance/hatches.json (overclockHatch).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A 200-tick recipe overclocked twice, with an EV Accelerate Hatch (44%) and a UHV Overclock Hatch:

\[ \begin{aligned} 200 \div 3 \div 3 &= 22.2\ \text{ticks} && \text{(two overclock steps with divisor 3)} \\ 22.2 \times 0.44 &= 9.8\ \text{ticks} && \text{(Accelerate Hatch)} \end{aligned} \]

Without the Overclock Hatch the same recipe takes \(200 \div 2 \div 2 \times 0.44 = 22\) ticks.

docs.title: Thread Hatch
docs.text:
Lets a multiblock run different recipes at the same time. A Parallel Hatch repeats one recipe; a Thread Hatch adds independent recipe slots, each with its own timer.

Hatch Extra threads Total ZPM +1 2 UV +3 4 UHV +7 8 UEV +15 16 UIV +31 32 UXV +63 64 OpV +127 128 MAX +255 256

You can lower the number in the hatch UI. Values are in config/gtna/balance/hatches.json (threadHatch).

docs.title: Where it works
docs.text: Threads work in machines built on GTNA's multiple-recipes logic whose structure has a slot for the hatch, for example the Industrial Slaughterhouse, the Integrated Ore Processor and its advanced version, the Mega Distillery, the Dimensionally Transcendent Dirt Forge, the Primitive Stone Furnace and the Advanced Fusion Reactor's cross-recipe module. Packs can build more on that base with KubeJS.

docs.title: How threads share parallel
docs.text: With a Parallel Hatch, the parallel is split between the threads. Example: a UEV Parallel Control Hatch (4,096) and a UV Thread Hatch (4 threads) give 4 recipes with 1,024 parallel each.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
The mechanics that tie GTNA's machines together, roughly in the order you meet them.

System Era In short Wireless steam network Steam one steam pool per player, no pipes Hydraulic components Steam the crafting parts of the steam age Modules and Structure Terminal all optional extra structures, and a tool that builds structures for you Nexus energy network LV onward wireless EU with a Flux Matrix as storage ME Pattern Buffers with AE2 patterns, inputs and modes in one multiblock part Void mining Steam, EV and later ores and fluids without digging Research engine pack-defined a research tree that modpacks fill with their own nodes Item effects — animated icons of the endgame materials

docs.title: Endgame
docs.text: System Tier In short Bose-Einstein Condensate UIV a network of condensate and nanites for the hardest crafts Space Elevator UHV orbital modules: assembly, asteroid mining, gas collection Nano Forge — builds nanites; four tiers Dyson Sphere — a swarm around the star, turned into laser power Eye of Harmony UXV mines a whole planet per run Forge of the Gods UIV an artificial star feeding up to 16 processing modules

docs.title: Bose-Einstein Condensate
docs.text: A late-game crafting network ported from GT: New Horizons. Five multiblocks share condensate, an exotic resource made from molten metals, and use it with nanites to craft Condensate Assembly recipes.

docs.title: The network
docs.text:
The machines are linked by BEC Conduits. Dye conduits to split one network into several. Condensate is a network resource, like energy in a cable: it never sits in a hatch.

Machine Role Entanglement Apparatus turns molten metals and fluids into condensate, all fluids in its hatches at once. Parallel fills the available EU/t; the cycle lasts as long as the slowest recipe. Condensate is voided if the network has no room Containment Field stores condensate (see below) Maxwell Gate lets condensate flow one way, with per-type filters set by fluid input hatches. Uses 1A UIV while active and blocks the network while off Observation Array feeds Teleportation Nodes linked by Line-of-Sight connectors with nanites, EU and condensate. One array serves many nodes. The nanite tier is the lowest among its buses; at most 30,720 nanites count Teleportation Node crafts the recipes with its own buses (see below)

docs.title: Crafting
docs.text:
The Teleportation Node crafts Condensate Assembly recipes:

  • Each item slot asks for one nanite tier at a time.
  • Extra nanites speed the craft up linearly. Higher-tier nanites than required slow it down by \(2^{\,\text{supplied} - \text{required}}\).
  • Condensate may arrive any time before the end of the craft. If it is still missing at the end, the craft fails.
  • More than 3 condensate types the recipe did not ask for also fail the craft.
  • No overclock. Minimum and maximum parallel and a speed divisor are set in the node's parameters.
  • Nodes stall while their Observation Array lacks EU.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
In the Containment Field, 1 field strength stores 1 mB and costs 1 EU/t. Injected condensate is split between fields by capacity. Above capacity a field keeps 9/10 of each condensate per second.

Power loss

A Containment Field that loses power or is switched off voids everything it holds.

docs.title: Dyson Sphere
docs.text:
Two multiblocks build a swarm of collectors around a planet's star and turn it into laser power.

Machine Role Launch Silo launches Dyson Swarm Modules into orbit of the planet it stands on. Surface only, not in orbit. Launch time grows with the planet's distance Receiving Station turns the swarm into power and sends it out as a laser. Needs computation and liquid helium

docs.title: Formulas
docs.text:
\[\text{EU/t} = V_{\text{MAX}} \cdot \text{modules} \cdot \frac{50 - \max(0,\ \text{damage} - 60)}{50}\]
  • Each station cycle adds 1 damage to the swarm. Above 99 damage the swarm loses a module.
  • A launch while damage is above 60 repairs the swarm instead of adding a module.
  • Up to 100,000 modules per planet.

Keep launching to keep damage below 60 and the output at full power.

docs.title: Eye of Harmony
docs.text:
The Eye of Harmony simulates a miniature universe and extracts the ores of a whole planet. Each run is expensive, slow and may fail; this page shows every calculation the controller makes.

Tier UXV Energy wireless (Nexus network) Origin port of GT5-Unofficial a3e1e112

docs.title: Planetary programs
docs.text:
The planet item in the controller slot picks the program. Products come from the GTCEu ore veins registered in that dimension. Packs add planets through KubeJS (GTNAStartupEvents.eyeOfHarmony). Planets beyond the Minecraft dimensions need Ad Astra.

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{base duration} &= 18000\ \text{s} \cdot 1.4^{\text{tier}} \\ \text{each gas (H and He)} &= 10^{9} \cdot (\text{tier} + 1)\ \text{mB} \\ \text{base chance} &= 1 - 0.05 \cdot \text{tier} \\ \text{return} &= \text{cost} \cdot (0.6 + \text{tier}/10) \\ \text{cost} &= \text{plasmas} + \text{ticks} \cdot (2^{19} + 10^{11})\ \text{EU} \end{aligned} \] Planet Tier Base duration H and He (mB) Base chance Cost without plasmas (EU) Overworld, Nether, End 0 5 h 1e9 100% 3.6e16 Moon 1 7 h 2e9 95% 5.04e16 Mars 2 9.80 h 3e9 90% 7.06e16 Venus, Mercury 4 19.21 h 5e9 80% 1.38e17 Glacio 5 26.89 h 6e9 75% 1.94e17

docs.title: Fields and circuit
docs.text:
Three fields of tier 0 to 8 (compression \(c\), acceleration \(a\), stabilisation \(s\)) and a circuit \(k\) from 0 to 24:

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{duration} &= \max\!\left(T \cdot 2^{-a} \cdot 0.97^{\,c - r} \cdot 2^{-k},\ 1\right) && r = \text{program minimum compression} \\ \text{startup cost} &= \text{cost} \cdot 4^{k} \\ \text{return} &= \text{base return} \cdot \left(1 - (8 - s) \cdot 0.05\right) && \text{does not scale with the circuit} \\ \text{chance} &= \text{base chance} - 0.0925\,a + 0.05\,s - \text{gas penalties} \\ \text{yield} &= 1 - 0.05\,s - \text{gas penalties} \\ \text{gas penalty} &= 1 - \exp\!\left(-\left(30 \cdot \left(\tfrac{\text{stored}}{\text{required}} - 1\right)\right)^{2}\right) \end{aligned} \] a / s Chance (Overworld) Yield Time 0 / 0 100% 100% ÷1 2 / 2 91.50% 90% ÷4 4 / 4 83% 80% ÷16 6 / 6 74.50% 70% ÷64 8 / 8 66% 60% ÷256 8 / 0 26% 100% ÷256 0 / 8 100% 60% ÷1

Excess gas also reduces chance and yield: storing 10% more already costs 99.99% per gas. Deliver the exact amount.

docs.title: Failure and pity
docs.text:
• A failure still returns the EU and produces SpaceTime: \(\text{chance} \cdot 14400 \cdot 2^{\text{tier} + 1}\) mB.
  • Consecutive failures under the same conditions build pity: \((1 - \text{chance}) \cdot \text{chance}\) per failure. Changing fields or circuit resets it.
  • The result is rolled at startup and saved: breaking the controller or reloading the world does not change it.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The controller consumes all stored hydrogen and helium at startup, excess included.
  • The return arrives through the Nexus network in parts; network loss is shown separately in the GUI.
  • A full output never loses anything: the cycle waits.

docs.title: Forge of the Gods
docs.text:
Image: GTNH Wiki, CC BY-SA 4.0.

The Forge of the Gods (Godforge) is a UIV multiblock that keeps an artificial star and powers up to 16 processing modules with wireless energy. This page collects what the game does not show: every formula, tables computed from the GTNA code, and the differences from GTNH.

Tier UIV Size 186 × 127 × 29 (ring 1) Energy wireless, no energy hatch Overclock imperfect (4/2), 4/2.3 with GGEBE Origin port of GT5-Unofficial a3e1e112

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Up to three rings. Modules sit in smaller rings around them. To build a new ring, turn the animation off (screwdriver on the controller or the cosmetics button), build it, and turn it back on with a soft mallet. The hologram projector uses the stack size to pick how many rings to show.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Module Unlock Base parallel Function Helioflare Power Forge START 1024 blast furnace or multi-smelter (furnace mode does not count for milestones) Helioflux Melting Core FDIM 512 blast furnace with molten output Heliothermal Plasma Fabricator GPCI 512 dust or fluid straight to plasma Heliofusion Exoticizer QGPIU (magmatter: EE) 64 quark-gluon plasma and MagMatter; needs automation

Module limit: 8, 12 with ring 2 (CD), 16 with ring 3 (EE). Going over the limit disconnects every module.

docs.title: Fuel
docs.text:
The star is lit with Stellar Fuel in the input bus. Startup cost: \(f \cdot 25 \cdot 1.2^{f}\) items. The consumption factor \(f\) goes up to 5 without upgrades. The controller drains fuel every 5 s (×2 while the battery charges).

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{DTR (residue)} &= f \cdot 300 \cdot 1.15^{f} && (\times 0.8 \text{ with STEM}) \\ \text{Stellar plasma} &= f \cdot 2 \cdot 1.08^{f} && (\times 0.8 \text{ with STEM}) \\ \text{MCSM} &= f / 25 \\ \text{heat} &= 12601 + 1000 \cdot \log_{1.5} f && (\text{base } 1.12 / 1.18 \text{ with SEFCP}) \end{aligned} \] f Base heat (K) Startup (items) DTR/s DTR/s with STEM Stellar plasma/s MCSM/s 1 12,601 30 345 276 2.16 0.04 2 14,310 72 793 635 4.67 0.08 3 15,310 129 1,369 1,095 7.56 0.12 4 16,020 207 2,099 1,679 10.88 0.16 5 16,570 311 3,017 2,414 14.69 0.20 6 17,020 447 4,164 3,331 19.04 0.24 10 18,279 1,547 12,137 9,709 43.18 0.40 20 19,989 19,168 98,199 78,559 186 0.80 43 21,877 2,730,247 5,255,292 4,204,234 2,354 1.72 70 23,079 6.11e8 3.72e8 2.98e8 30,605 2.80

Max factors with TSE: residue 70 (72 with STEM), stellar plasma 181 (184 with STEM), MCSM uncapped. Above 43 the effective SA factor grows slowly: \(43 + (f - 43)^{0.4}\).

docs.title: Heat and bonus cap
docs.text: Heat bonuses apply up to the cap: 15,000 K, or 30,000 K with CNTI. With NDPE, heat above 30,000 K counts compressed: \(30000 + (\text{heat} - 30000)^{e}\), with e = 0.85 for the Power Forge and 0.8 for the others.

docs.title: Parallel
docs.text:
\[ \begin{aligned} \text{parallel} &= \text{base} \cdot \text{CTCDD}(\times 2) \cdot \text{SA} \cdot \text{EPEC} \cdot \text{PoS} \\ \text{SA} &= 1 + f_{\text{eff}} / 15 && (\text{TCT: } \times 3 \text{ on Melting Core and Power Forge with DoP, } \times 2 \text{ otherwise}) \\ \text{EPEC} &= 1 + \text{heat} / 15000 && (\text{Melting Core, Power Forge with DoP; otherwise } 1 + \text{heat}/25000) \\ \text{PoS} &= 1 + \text{upgrades} / 5 && (\text{Melting Core, Power Forge with DoP; otherwise } 1 + \text{upgrades}/8) \end{aligned} \]

Exoticizer: square root of the total with PA, otherwise 1.

f f eff. SA SA + TCT (Melting Core) 5 5 1.33 4 15 15 2 6 43 43 3.87 11.60 70 46 4.07 12.20 181 50 4.33 13 1000 58 4.87 14.60

The GTNH wiki only shows the /15000 and /5 versions. The code uses larger divisors outside the Melting Core.

docs.title: Speed and energy
docs.text: \[ \begin{aligned} \text{IGCC:}\quad & t \times \text{heat}^{-0.01} \\ \text{DoR:}\quad & t \div \text{parallel}^{0.02} \text{ (plasma) or } \text{parallel}^{0.012} \text{ (others)} \\ \text{REC:}\quad & \text{discount} = \frac{1 - 1.05^{-0.05 \cdot \text{max battery}}}{20} \\ \text{IMKG:}\quad & \text{charge discount} = 1 - \left(-0.6\,(c - 0.5)^2 + 0.15\right) \text{ on plasma, } \times \tfrac{2}{3} \text{ on the others} \\ \text{GISS:}\quad & V \mathrel{+}= \text{fuel units/s} \cdot 10^{8}\ \text{EU/t} \\ \text{NGMS:}\quad & V \times 4 \text{ per active ring (applied last)} \end{aligned} \]

docs.title: Milestones
docs.text:
Each milestone has 7 tiers and grants graviton shards equal to the tier. Once all four reach tier 7, Inversion removes the cap and every new tier costs the same as tier 7.

docs.text:
Bought with graviton shards. Blue line: one prerequisite is enough; red line: all of them are needed. After the Exoticizer the tree splits in three (purple: heat; orange: parallel; green: plasma). One branch first, the second with ring 2, all three with ring 3. Refunds work only when no dependent upgrade is active.

docs.title: Differences from GTNH
docs.text:
• Plasma Fabricator base parallel is 512 in the code (the GTNH wiki says 384).
  • Exoticizer magmatter is unlocked by EE in the GTNA code (the GTNH wiki says END).
  • Material costs adapted to items that exist in GTNA (previous section).
  • Fuels and max factors are identical to GT5-Unofficial a3e1e112.

docs.title: Hydraulic components
docs.text:
GTNA's steam age has its own crafting components, the hydraulic parts. They play the role of electric motors, pistons and pumps in the recipes of GTNA's steam multiblocks, the wireless steam hatches and the Steam Elevator.

Component Used in Hydraulic Motor the other hydraulic parts; Stone Superheater; Large Steam Ore Washer, Mixer, Centrifuge and Thermal Centrifuge Hydraulic Piston Hydraulic Arm; Large Steam Hammer, Compressor, Extractor, Lathe, Extruder and Sifter Hydraulic Pump Hydraulic Steam Receiver; Large Steam Extractor, Ore Washer and Bath; Primitive Distillation Tower; Steam Cracker Hydraulic Arm Steam Manufacturer; Large Steam Cutting Machine; Steam Elevator greenhouse and bee modules Hydraulic Conveyor Large Steam Alloy Smelter, Bath, Cutting Machine, Bending Machine, Extruder and Wiremill Hydraulic Regulator wireless steam hatches; Cactus Wonder; tier II and III Steam Elevator modules Hydraulic Vapor Generator tier III Steam Elevator modules; Compact Hyper Pressure Reactor Hydraulic Steam Jet Spewer Hydraulic Vapor Generator; Steam Elevator and its tier I modules; Steam Item Vault Hydraulic Steam Receiver Steam Elevator modules; Void Miner SteamGate Aged Precision Steam Component most Large Steam multiblocks (Crusher, Furnace, Hammer, Compressor, Extractor, Ore Washer…)

docs.title: Two ways to make them
docs.text:
• Crafting table: the first parts have shaped recipes made of Clay Compound plates, iron rods and rotors, bronze gears and tiny bronze fluid pipes.
  • Hydraulic Manufacturing: the same parts in the Steam Manufacturer. It runs on steam (16 mB/t per parallel) and processes many at once. The steel wireless steam hatches and the Steam Elevator are made here too.

JEI/EMI lists every recipe under Hydraulic Manufacturing.

docs.title: Item effects
docs.text:
GTNA's endgame materials have animated icons: halos, glowing outlines and three shaders. GTNA draws them itself; RenderBlender is no longer needed (since 0.5.6).

Effect Look Where Halo soft tinted disc behind the icon inventories Glow edge tinted, slightly larger copy of the icon behind it inventories Cosmic drifting star field inside the icon item icon Eternal slow flowing light bands with sparkles item icon Unstable flickering, crackling noise item icon

docs.title: Turning them down
docs.text:
In config/gtna.yaml, client section:

Option Default Effect itemHalo true draws halos itemGlowEdge true draws glow edges itemShaderEffects true draws the cosmic, eternal and unstable shaders itemEffectSpeed 100 animation speed in percent, 0 to 400 (0 freezes it)

docs.title: For pack and resource pack authors
docs.text:
Item models: five model loaders, gtna:halo, gtna:glow_edge, gtna:cosmic, gtna:eternal and gtna:unstable, add an effect to any item model.

KubeJS (kubejs/client_scripts, runs again on every F3+T):

GTNAClientEvents.itemEffects(event => {
  // every form of a GTCEu material
  event.material('gtna:advanced_nitinol').halo(0xFF66CCFF, 8).pulse(true)
  // one item; replaces the effects of its model
  event.item('kubejs:my_core').cosmic().colors(0xFF050418, 0xFF7FD4FF).glowEdge(0xFFFFAA00, 1.5)
  event.item('gtceu:gtna_spacetime_ingot').eternal().mask('gtna:mask/cosmic').speed(0.5)
  event.item('gtceu:gtna_chaos_matter_dust').clear()
})
Method Meaning halo(argb, size) halo with a radius in item pixels glowEdge(argb), glowEdge(argb, width) outline glow cosmic(), eternal(), unstable() shader effect color(argb), colors(primary, secondary) tint; 0 keeps the default palette pulse(true) makes the halo pulse speed(x) animation speed multiplier mask(texture), texture(texture) shader mask or halo texture; by default the item's own shape clear() removes every effect from the item

docs.title: Auxiliary modules
docs.text:
Some multiblocks accept an auxiliary module: an optional extra structure built next to the main one and checked by the same controller. The machine forms without it. When the module forms, the hatches found in it are added to the machine, which unlocks new hatch types or new recipe types. The controller shows Formed modules: n / total, JEI/EMI shows each module as an extra page of the structure preview, and the item tooltip lists what the module unlocks.

Machine What the module adds Electric Blast Furnace (GTCEu) Accelerate Hatch and extra wired Energy Hatches Liquefaction Furnace Parallel Hatch and Accelerate Hatch Evaporation Plant Parallel Hatch and Accelerate Hatch Cold Ice Freezer Atomization Condensation recipes, an Accelerate Hatch and up to six extra Energy Hatches Component Assembler two extension shapes (normal and wide) with more hatches Rocket Large Turbine 2× output, +20% efficiency, 2× rotor damage, up to three extra Energy Output Hatches Supercritical Steam Turbine same bonuses as the Rocket Large Turbine module Advanced Fusion Reactor four tier modules (MK-II to MK-V) and a cross-recipe module Nano Forge the tier 2, 3 and 4 structures

Modpacks can add modules to any multiblock, GTNA's or another mod's, with KubeJS: see GTNAServerEvents.subPatterns. The module registry lives in GTIA Lib since GTNA 0.6.1.

docs.title: Nexus Structure Terminal
docs.text:
A builder for big multiblocks.

  • Right-click in the air: settings.
  • Shift + right-click a controller: builds the structure around it, modules included.
Setting Effect Blocks by tier pick the coil, casing or glass tier to place, per category Repetitions (0–1000) layers for expandable structures such as a distillation tower Module build (0–100) how many module layers to build No Hatch skips buses and hatches, so you can place them yourself Replace swaps blocks already in place (coils of another tier, for example) for your choice; the old blocks go to your inventory Mirror builds the mirrored version of the structure Demolition clears blocks that stand where the structure needs air

In survival the terminal takes blocks from your inventory. Right-click an AE2 Wireless Access Point with it to also take blocks from that ME network while you are in range.

docs.title: Nano Forge
docs.text: Builds nanites with huge amounts of power. Ported from GT: New Horizons.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
The nanite in any input bus sets the forge's tier and is never consumed. Each tier also needs a bigger structure; the extra parts are auxiliary modules, so JEI/EMI shows each tier as its own preview page.

Tier Nanite in the bus 1 Carbon Nanites 2 Neutronium Nanites 3 Transcendent Metal Nanites 4 MagMatter Nanites

Recipes below the forge's tier get perfect overclock.

docs.title: Tier 4: MagMatter
docs.text:
With a nanite equal to the recipe's output in the bus, the forge drains all molten MagMatter in its hatches and turns it into parallel:

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{parallel} &= \frac{\text{MagMatter}}{288 / 2^{\,4 - \text{recipe tier}}} \\ \text{duration} &\times 0.9999^{\text{parallel}} \end{aligned} \]

docs.title: Nexus energy network
docs.text: GTNA's wireless EU network. Generators push EU into a personal balance and machines pull from it, at any distance, with no cables. The Nexus Flux Matrix multiblock sets how much the network can hold.

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
Part What it does Nexus Flux Matrix the storage: its Nexus Capacitors set the capacity Wireless Energy Hatch pulls EU from the network into a multiblock. LV to MAX, 1A to 1,048,576A (powers of 4) Wireless Dynamo Hatch pushes a generator's EU into the network. Same tiers and amperages Wireless Energy Network Input / Output Terminal multiblock parts that charge a recipe's EU straight from the network, or send generated EU straight to it, up to 9.2 × 10¹⁸ EU per run Generator Array runs up to four GTCEu generators and sends their output to the network Nexus Linker links hatches to a network that is not yours Quantum Network Terminal handheld monitor: stored EU, input, output and loss per tick, connections

A hatch's internal buffer holds V × 64 × A EU. Every hatch binds to the player who placed it: there is nothing to link in single player.

docs.title: The Flux Matrix
docs.text:
The Matrix is a 7 × 7 frame whose middle repeats from 2 to 30 layers. Each layer holds 25 Nexus Capacitors, so a Matrix has 50 to 750 capacitors.

  • Capacity is the sum of the capacitors.
  • Efficiency and the transfer number use the average capacitor tier (or the highest one, with machines.nexusFluxMatrix.useHighestTierForEfficiency).
  • 750 MAX capacitors make the network unlimited: no capacity cap and no transfer cap.
  • Energy you deposit stays as your balance even if the Matrix is broken.
Capacitor EU per block Transfer (EU/t) Works across dimensions LV 160,000 2,000 no MV 1,500,000 8,000 no HV 10,000,000 32,000 no EV 50,000,000 128,000 yes IV 250,000,000 512,000 yes LuV 1.5 × 10⁹ 2,048,000 yes ZPM 1.5 × 10¹⁰ 8,192,000 yes UV 1.5 × 10¹¹ 32,768,000 yes UHV 3 × 10¹² 131,072,000 yes UEV 5 × 10¹³ 524,288,000 yes UIV 9 × 10¹⁴ 2,097,152,000 yes UXV 1.5 × 10¹⁶ 8,388,608,000 yes OpV 2.5 × 10¹⁷ 33,554,432,000 yes MAX 5 × 10¹⁸ 5 × 10²³ yes

Values are the defaults of config/gtna/balance/nexus_flux_matrix.json; a modpack can change any of them. Below EV average tier, hatches only reach the network from the Matrix's own dimension. The transfer number caps what a Generator Array sends per tick.

docs.title: Loss
docs.text:
The balance file also picks where energy is lost:

lossApplication Behaviour LEGACY (default) no loss on the network. The Generator Array keeps its own 5% loss. The Matrix GUI shows an efficiency from 85% (LV) to 100% (MAX) as information MATRIX_INPUT_ONCE each deposit loses a percentage set by the average capacitor tier: 5% LV, 4% MV, 3% HV, 2% EV, 1% IV, 0% from LuV. The network only works while a Matrix is formed NO_LOSS nothing is lost

The loss is charged once, when EU enters the network, with exact accounting: fractions carry over to the next deposit instead of being rounded away.

docs.title: Setting it up
docs.text:
1. Build the Nexus Flux Matrix and fill its middle with capacitors.
  2. Put Wireless Dynamo Hatches on generators (or build a Generator Array).
  3. Put Wireless Energy Hatches on machines.
  4. Check the balance with the Quantum Network Terminal or the HUD (client.wirelessEnergyHud).

To use a friend's network: Shift + right-click their Matrix with the Nexus Linker to copy it, then right-click each hatch. Shift + right-click a hatch to unbind it.

docs.title: ME Pattern Buffers
docs.text: A Pattern Buffer is a multiblock part that holds AE2 processing patterns and acts as input bus, input hatch and pattern provider at once. Put one on a GTCEu or GTNA multiblock and AE2 can send it crafting jobs directly. Requires Applied Energistics 2.

docs.title: The four buffers
docs.text:
Buffer Pattern slots (default) ME Mini Pattern Buffer 9 ME Pattern Buffer 21 ME Advanced Pattern Buffer 32 ME Ultimate Pattern Buffer 72

The GUI shows 90 slots per page. Slot counts come from config/gtna/balance/pattern_buffers.json (1 to 540 per buffer) and are read at startup.

Upgrade cards turn a buffer into the next one in place, keeping patterns, slot settings and stored items: the Expansion Card (21 slots), the Precision Card (32) and the Ascension Card (72). Copy and Cut cards move a whole configuration: sneak-right-click a buffer to take it, right-click another to paste it. A broken buffer keeps its patterns and slot data.

docs.title: Per-slot settings
docs.text:
Middle-click a pattern slot to edit it:

  • Circuit: a programmed circuit for that pattern only. Embed Circuit in the tools tab writes one circuit into every pattern (optionally skipping patterns that already have one).
  • Catalyst items and fluids: kept in the slot and never consumed, such as molds, lenses or a catalyst fluid.
  • Ghost items and fluids: extra inputs added to the pattern with your own amounts.
  • Preferred mode: for multiblocks with several recipe types, the mode this pattern should run in. With machines.bufferDrivenMachineMode on (default), the buffer switches a GTCEu machine's mode while it is idle, so one Large Cutter can cut and lathe from the same buffer.
  • Recipe cache: the buffer remembers which recipe each slot resolved to. Clear it after you change recipes with scripts.

A buffer mode at the top limits the whole buffer to one recipe type.

docs.title: Related parts
docs.text: Part What it does ME Pattern Buffer Proxy lets a second multiblock use the patterns of a buffer elsewhere. Shift-right-click the buffer with a Data Stick, then right-click the proxy. Same dimension, and the buffer's chunk must be loaded ME Export Buffer output bus and output hatch in one block: sends items and fluids straight to the ME network. Its internal buffer holds up to 9.2 × 10¹⁸ of each item or fluid, so recipes never stall on a full output Nexus Craft Pattern Hatch takes crafting-table patterns for the Nexus Assembly Forge ME Storage Access Hatch / Big Storage Access Hatch connects the ME Storage multiblock to an AE2 network; the big version counts beyond 64-bit

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• One buffer per production line is easier to read than one huge buffer: AE2's Pattern Access Terminal lists each buffer separately. A buffer can also be hidden from that terminal.
  • If a pattern does nothing, open the slot: a missing circuit or a wrong preferred mode is the usual cause.
  • When a modpack lowers the slot count, GTNA keeps the old size for buffers already in the world (pattern_buffer_capacity_history.json). Keep that file with the world.

docs.title: Research engine
docs.text: A data-driven research tree that other systems can read. A modpack describes nodes in JSON; a team unlocks them by obtaining an item; a node can then gate machine recipes or switch flags that other code reads. GTNA ships the engine only. The nodes belong to the modpack.

docs.title: For players
docs.text:
• Press K (rebindable) to open the research tree. Nodes are grouped by tier; lines connect a node to its prerequisites. Green is unlocked, yellow is the next one you can unlock, grey is locked. Hover a node for what it needs and what it unlocks.
  • A node unlocks by itself once its prerequisites are met and you hold the item it asks for (crafting, picking up or machine output all count). One teammate holding it is enough for the whole team.
  • A gated recipe shows a red Research: line in EMI (green once unlocked), and a machine that cannot run it says Requires research: .

    Progress belongs to the player's effective FTB Team, or to the player when there is none, the same rule as fluid discoveries.

    Packs without research nodes can turn the whole tree off with gameplay.researchTree: false in config/gtna.yaml.

docs.title: For pack authors
docs.text:
Put one JSON file per node in data/<namespace>/gtna_research/. The node id is the file path: data/gtia/gtna_research/lv/aluminium.json is gtia:lv/aluminium.

{
  "tier": 2,
  "icon": "gtceu:aluminium_ingot",
  "prerequisites": ["gtia:lv/blast_furnace"],
  "trigger": { "type": "obtain_item", "item": "gtceu:aluminium_dust" },
  "grants": [
    { "type": "recipe_condition", "recipes": ["gtceu:electric_blast_furnace/blast_aluminium"] },
    { "type": "flag", "id": "gtia:aluminium" }
  ],
  "quest": "optional text, not used by the engine"
}
Field Meaning tier Column group in the tree, 1 or higher. Default 1. icon Item shown in the tree. Defaults to the trigger item. prerequisites Node ids that must be unlocked first. trigger obtain_item (unlocks when the team holds the item) or manual (commands and quests only). Default manual. requires_mods Optional list of mod ids. If any is missing the node is skipped silently, so a pack can ship nodes for optional mods. Do not make other nodes depend on it. grants recipe_condition blocks the listed recipe ids until the node is unlocked. flag sets a switch read by KnowledgeService.hasFlag.

Rules the loader enforces: a node with an unknown prerequisite, a prerequisite cycle or a tier below 1 is dropped and logged, together with everything that depends on it. A field that is present but invalid fails the whole node, instead of silently using a default.

Choose trigger items the player can reach without the node's own gate, or the node can never unlock. A good trigger is the machine or ingredient that shows the player is ready.

Names come from lang keys: gtna.research.node.<namespace>.<path with dots> (for the example, gtna.research.node.gtia.lv.aluminium), with an optional .desc key for the tooltip. Without a key, the id is shown.

A recipe with a gate runs only for an owner whose team holds the node. Crafting-table, AE2 and pattern recipes are not covered.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Who Effect /gtna research list [player] anyone (others need op) Unlocked and locked nodes. /gtna research info <node> anyone Tier and prerequisites. /gtna research unlock <player> <node> [force] op Unlock a node; force unlocks its whole prerequisite chain. /gtna research reset <player> op Clear the player's team progress.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• KnowledgeService: isUnlocked, unlock, hasFlag, recipeAllowed, reset. Server side.
  • KnowledgeUnlockedEvent is posted on the Forge bus when a scope newly unlocks a node.
  • FTB Quests: the Research node task type (gtna:research_node) completes when the node is unlocked. It is registered only when FTB Quests is installed.
  • The server sends the graph and the player's unlocked nodes to the client on login, after /reload and when progress changes.

An example datapack is in examples/datapack.

docs.title: Space Elevator
docs.text: A cable to orbit that powers up to 12 modules standing around its base. Ported from GT: New Horizons.

docs.title: Running the elevator
docs.text:
• It works only from UHV (above ZPM) and needs computation: \(128 \cdot (\text{tier} - \text{ZPM})\) CWU/t.
  • Feed 256 Nanotube Spools through its input bus.
  • The Power Modules in the structure set every module's parallel: \(4^{\,\text{MK} - 1}\). All Power Modules must be the same MK (I to V). The MK also decides which Assembler Module recipes can run.
Power Module Module parallel MK I 1 MK II 4 MK III 16 MK IV 64 MK V 256

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Module What it does Assembler Module assembles parts in orbit Resource Collection Module sends drones to mine 20 asteroid ore mixes and collect 11 gases, with MK I to VI drones and rocket fuel

Modules work only while their Space Elevator runs.

docs.title: Void mining
docs.text: Three machines produce ores and fluids without digging: a steam-era miner, an electric miner driven by vein essences, and a rig that keeps pumping a fluid deposit after you found it. They give raw materials only, so ore processing still matters.

docs.title: Void Miner SteamGate Aged (steam)
docs.text:
Catalog page. Mines a "steam dimension" for Raw Gold, Copper, Iron, Cobalt and Coal, with Drilling Fluid every run. Hotter steam in a fluid input hatch boosts it; the hottest fluid present wins:

Fluid in the hatch Items Speed Cost Steam 1× 1× 1× Dense Supercritical Steam 2× 2× 1.5× SuperHeated Steam 3× 3× 2× Insanely Supercritical Steam 5× 5× 4×

Multipliers are in config/gtna/balance/machines.json (voidMinerSteamGateAged).

docs.title: Electric Void Miner (EV)
docs.text:
Catalog page. Uses EU and Drilling Fluid every run. Pick a mode in the machine's mode tab:

  • Precise: consumes one essence and mines that vein. Circuit 1 runs the three EV programs (Iron/Copper, Tin/Lead, Gold/Silver); circuit 2 runs the 40 full vein programs ported from GregTech Leisure (LuV for Overworld and Nether veins, ZPM for End veins). Five planetary programs (Moon, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Glacio) need Ad Astra.
  • Random: no essence. Circuit 1 rolls the EV pool (Iron, Copper, Tin, Lead, Gold, Silver at 25% each); circuit 2 rolls the full pool at ZPM (2% each). Both use 10,000 mB of Drilling Fluid and 30 s.

EV runs one operation at a time. From IV, a Parallel Hatch adds parallel up to 1,024, limited by energy, fluid and output space. An Accelerate Hatch also fits.

docs.title: Making essences
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Bone Block + Biomass] -->|Chemical Bath HV| E[Essence]
    E -->|Mixer MV + 16 seeds + Distilled Water + CO₂| S[16 Essence Seeds]
    W[World Data Scanner] -->|scan in the target dimension| D[World data / Planet Data Chip]
    S --> I[Incubator HV]
    D -.->|not consumed| I
    O[Raw ore samples] --> I
    I -->|+ 10,000 mB Biomass and Milk| X[64 vein essences]

The World Data Scanner must stand in the dimension it scans (LV to IV for Overworld, Nether and End; EV on other planets). Data and planet chips are reusable. The Incubator needs the vein's raw ores as a sample, so the first ore still has to be mined some other way. The Large Incubator runs cultures in parallel.

Numbers are in config/gtna/balance/electric_void_miner.json: duration, EU/t, Drilling Fluid, output caps and parallel per tier.

docs.title: Void Fluid Drilling Rig (EV)
docs.text:
Catalog page. Keeps producing a fluid after you really extracted it from a natural deposit:

  1. Pump a deposit with the GTCEu Fluid Drilling Rig until it delivers fluid.
  2. Right-click that rig's controller with the Deposit Recorder, with a Data Stick in your inventory. You get reusable Deposit Data for that fluid and place.
  3. Put the data in the Void Rig's input bus and supply EU and Drilling Fluid.

Default cycle: 400 ticks, 1,920 EU/t, 100 mB Drilling Fluid. Output per cycle: Oil 2,000, Heavy Oil 1,500, Light Oil 2,500, Natural Gas 1,500 (also needs 100 mB Nitrogen), Salt Water 4,000, Raw Oil 2,000 mB. Parallel: EV 1, IV 2, LuV 4, ZPM 8, UV 16, doubling up to 1,024.

The rig works in the deposit's own dimension; a remote upgrade in the same bus lets it work elsewhere. Discoveries belong to your FTB team when FTB Teams is installed. Programs live in config/gtna/balance/void_fluid_drill.json.

docs.title: Infinity Fluid Drilling Rig (ZPM)
docs.text: Catalog page. A fluid drilling rig whose veins never deplete: 256× output at ZPM and 384× at UV.

docs.title: Wireless steam network
docs.text:
Every player has one steam pool that lives with the world. Output hatches put steam into it and input hatches take steam out, with no pipes, at any distance and across dimensions. It is GTNA's answer to the steam pipes of the early game.

Who owns the pool the player who placed the hatch Range unlimited, every dimension Pool size a 64-bit number (about 9.2 × 10¹⁸ mB) Saved with the world (gtna_steam_network) Origin GT: Not Leisure wireless steam hatches, rebuilt for GTCEu

docs.title: The hatches
docs.text:
Hatch Goes on Tank Recipe Wireless Steam Output Hatch the Large Steam Solar Boiler 128,000,000 mB crafting table: Bricked Bronze Casing, Hydraulic Regulators, Huge Stronze Fluid Pipes, LV Output Bus Wireless Steam Output Hatch Steel same 2,147,483,647 mB Hydraulic Manufacturing: bronze hatch + 8 Steel Drums Wireless Steam Input Hatch any multiblock that takes a steam hatch 100,000 mB crafting table: same as the output, with an LV Input Bus Wireless Steam Input Hatch Steel same 2,147,483,647 mB Hydraulic Manufacturing: bronze hatch + 8 Steel Drums

Tank sizes and an optional per-tick limit can be changed in config/gtna.yaml.

The output hatch only fits the Large Steam Solar Boiler

In GTNA 0.6.1 the Large Steam Solar Boiler is the only structure with a slot for the wireless output hatch. Single-block boilers cannot push steam into it: the hatch never accepts steam from pipes.

docs.title: How steam moves
docs.text:
graph LR
    B[Large Steam Solar Boiler] --> O(Wireless output hatch)
    O -->|whole tank, every tick| P{{Your steam pool}}
    P -->|fair share, every tick| I1(Input hatch)
    P --> I2(Input hatch)
    I1 --> M1[Steam multiblock]
    I2 --> M2[Steam multiblock]
  • Output: each tick the hatch moves its whole tank into the pool.
  • Input: each tick the hatch fills its free space from the pool, but takes at most a fair share: the balance divided by the number of input hatches that still have room. With a small pool every machine gets some steam, instead of the first one draining it all.
  • Payments are exact: the pool never goes negative and a full tank never voids steam.

docs.title: Watching the network
docs.text:
• /gtna steam prints your balance, the steam added and used since the server started, and every hatch connected in the last 2 seconds with its position, tier and last transfer.
  • HUD: turn on client.wirelessSteamHud to see the balance, the flow and a history graph on screen. Its position and graph length are in the same config section.
  • Jade shows the hatch's tank and its last transfer when you look at it.
Command Permission Effect /gtna steam everyone your own network report /gtna steam <player> op another player's report /gtna steam add <amount> op adds steam to your pool (negative values subtract) /gtna steam set <amount> op sets your pool

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Build the Large Steam Solar Boiler early and give it a wireless output hatch: one boiler can feed every steam multiblock of the base.
  • Upgrade input hatches to Steel when a machine stalls on steam: the bronze tank holds only 100,000 mB.
  • Steam belongs to the player who placed the hatch. On a server, have the same player place the hatches of a shared base.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
GTNA has two kinds of settings:

  • config/gtna.yaml: gameplay, client and per-machine switches. Every option also shows up in the in-game config menu, with a comment.
  • config/gtna/balance/*.json: balance numbers for modpacks. They are read at startup; restart the game or server after editing.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
The game stops with a missing dependency message

GTNA 0.6.1 needs GTCEu 7.5.3 or newer and GTIA Lib 0.5.0 or newer. An older GTCEu caused crashes like NoSuchFieldError: CLUSTER_MAX_HARVESTABLES (issue #1). Update both mods. See Installation.

GTNA material icons show as missing textures

GTNA 0.5.4 and 0.5.5 depended on RenderBlender for those models. Update to 0.5.6 or newer, which draws the effects itself.

Can I turn the item effects (halos, shaders) off?

Yes, in config/gtna.yaml, client section: itemHalo, itemGlowEdge, itemShaderEffects and itemEffectSpeed. See Item effects.

My structure does not form

Open the structure in JEI/EMI and compare layer by layer; hover each position to see what fits there. Check that every casing has the same tier where the machine asks for it (steam machines in high-pressure mode need all casings in steel). The Nexus Structure Terminal can build it for you.

The wireless steam output hatch does nothing on my boiler

It only fits the Large Steam Solar Boiler and never accepts steam from pipes. See Wireless steam network.

A Pattern Buffer pattern never runs

Middle-click the slot: a missing programmed circuit or the wrong preferred mode is the usual cause. See ME Pattern Buffers.

The recipes are different from GTNH or GTO

GTNA ships working default recipes. Balance belongs to the modpack, which can change them through KubeJS, datapacks and the balance files in config/gtna/balance/.

Do I need Ad Astra?

No. Without it the Steam Elevator cannot travel, the Eye of Harmony only has the Minecraft dimensions and the planetary void mining programs are missing.

Where do I report a bug?

On the issue tracker, with latest.log (and crash-reports/ if the game crashed) and the versions of GTNA, GTCEu and GTIA Lib.

Can I translate the wiki or the mod?

Yes, see Translating.

docs.title: First steps
docs.text:
GTNA follows GregTech's tiers. This is roughly the order in which its content shows up. A modpack can change every recipe, so your pack's quest book has the final say.

Stage What GTNA adds Read Steam large steam machines, hydraulic parts, the Large Steam Solar Boiler, wireless steam, primitive machines with no energy, the Steam Elevator Steam age, Wireless steam network LV–HV Nexus energy network, Industrial Slaughterhouse, Accelerate Hatches, more processing multiblocks Nexus energy network, Industrial Slaughterhouse EV–IV Electric Void Miner and Void Fluid Drilling Rig, Pattern Buffers at scale, auxiliary modules Void mining, ME Pattern Buffers LuV–UV mega machines, Thread and Overclock Hatches, data and computation Hatches and parts UHV–UXV Space Elevator, Nano Forge, Dyson Sphere, Eye of Harmony, original multiblocks Systems UIV–MAX Bose-Einstein Condensate, Forge of the Gods, Stellar Containment Chamber Forge of the Gods

docs.title: Habits that help
docs.text:
• Read the controller tooltip. Every GTNA machine says what it does, its parallel and its quirks; the last line names the mod it was ported from.
  • Look at the structure in JEI/EMI before building. Hover a position to see which blocks and hatches fit there.
  • Let the terminal build it. The Nexus Structure Terminal places big structures for you.
  • Check the catalog when you meet a new machine: 170 pages with block lists.
  • Use the wireless networks early. Steam and EU without pipes or cables save a lot of building.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Mod Version Minecraft 1.20.1 required Forge 47.4.1 or newer required GregTech CEu Modern 7.5.3 or newer required; Forge stops with a message if it is older GTIA Lib 0.5.0 or newer required since GTNA 0.6.1 Applied Energistics 2 for 1.20.1 (tested with 15.4.10) required: the ME parts are always registered JEI or EMI any recent optional, strongly recommended: recipes and structure previews KubeJS 2001.6.5 optional: scripting API Ad Astra 1.15.20 or newer optional: planets for the Steam Elevator, the Eye of Harmony and the planetary void mining programs FTB Teams / FTB Quests — optional: team progress for research and fluid discoveries, research quest task Productive Bees — optional: the Steam Elevator Bee Breeding module Jade — optional: wireless steam hatch details

GTCEu needs its own dependencies (such as LDLib); install the versions its download page asks for. RenderBlender is not needed since GTNA 0.5.6.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Forge 47.4.1 or newer for Minecraft 1.20.1.
  2. Put GTCEu, GTIA Lib, Applied Energistics 2 and GTNA in the mods folder.
  3. Add the optional mods you want.
  4. Start the game once. GTNA writes config/gtna.yaml and the balance files in config/gtna/balance/ (see Configuration).

Downloads: GitHub releases. Developers can also get release jars from the organisation's Maven.

docs.title: Servers
docs.text: GTNA runs on dedicated servers. Install the same mods on the server and on every client; client-only options (HUDs, item effects) stay in each player's config/gtna.yaml.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Only machines the author asked for are ported, from the named source (GTO, GTL, GTNL, TST, GTNH).
  • Each port brings its original structure, mechanics and textures, with KubeJS support.
  • Default recipes are a baseline; balance belongs to the modpack.

docs.title: Pressurized Water Reactor (planned)
docs.text:
Not in the game yet

The design is approved; the code has not started. Numbers below are the design targets and may change in balancing.

A fission reactor for the IV age, with the physics of a real PWR on a game time and power scale. It makes high-pressure steam; separate turbines turn it into EU. Hard to design, easy to run: everything that needs constant attention has an automatic mode set once (power setpoint, boron program, refuelling campaign).

Tier IV (all blocks and parts from the IV age: tungstensteel, Inconel 625, Hastelloy-N, boron carbide, PBI) Rated power 131,072 EU/t thermal (16 A IV), 262,144 L/t of steam Structure containment about 47 × 48 × 47, plus a 66-block cooling tower Core 37 fuel channels, 5 control rod banks, 4 steam generators, 4 primary pumps, pressurizer

docs.title: Fuel
docs.text:
Each channel takes a fuel assembly with enrichment \(e\) (%) and burnup \(B\) (GWd/t):

\[ \begin{aligned} k_\infty(e, B) &= k_0(e) - 0.006\,B, \qquad k_0(e) = 0.92 + 0.075\,e \\ k_{\text{core}} &= 0.97 \cdot \overline{k_\infty} \quad \text{(neutron leakage)} \end{aligned} \] Assembly \(e\) (%) \(k_0\) Max burnup (GWd/t) LEU-3 3 1.15 19 LEU-4 4 1.22 31.5 LEU-4.5 4.5 1.26 37.8 LEU-5 5 1.29 44

Gadolinia assemblies (burnable absorber) and, at LuV, MOX from PUREX-recycled plutonium.

docs.title: Reactivity
docs.text:
\[ \begin{aligned} \rho &= \frac{k - 1}{k} \quad (1\ \text{pcm} = 10^{-5}) \\ \rho_{\text{total}} &= \rho_{\text{fuel}} + \rho_{\text{rods}} + \rho_{\text{boron}} + \rho_{\text{Doppler}} + \rho_{\text{mod}} + \rho_{\text{Xe}} + \rho_{\text{Sm}} \\ \rho_{\text{rods}} &= -8000\ \text{pcm} \cdot \left(x - \frac{\sin 2\pi x}{2\pi}\right) \\ \rho_{\text{boron}} &= -10\ \text{pcm/ppm} \cdot C_B \\ \rho_{\text{Doppler}} &= -2.5\ \text{pcm/K} \cdot (T_{\text{fuel}} - 565\ \text{K}), \qquad \rho_{\text{mod}} = -40\ \text{pcm/K} \cdot (T_{\text{mod}} - 565\ \text{K}) \end{aligned} \]

Both temperature coefficients are negative, so the reactor regulates itself. Rods are worth little at the ends and a lot in the middle (the real S curve).

docs.title: Kinetics
docs.text:
Point kinetics with one delayed-neutron group: \(\beta = 650\) pcm, \(\Lambda = 2 \times 10^{-5}\) s, \(\lambda = 0.08\ \text{s}^{-1}\).

\[ \frac{dn}{dt} = \frac{\rho - \beta}{\Lambda}\,n + \lambda C, \qquad \frac{dC}{dt} = \frac{\beta}{\Lambda}\,n - \lambda C, \qquad \tau \approx \frac{\beta - \rho}{\lambda\,\rho} \]

Above \(\beta\) the reactor is prompt critical; an automatic SCRAM on short period (< 10 s) keeps normal operation far from it.

docs.title: Xenon
docs.text:
Real I-135 → Xe-135 chain with time compressed (1 real hour = 1 game minute). After a shutdown xenon rises for about 10 minutes before falling (the xenon pit); the automatic mode shows how long until a restart is possible.

\[ \frac{dI}{dt} = \gamma_I \Sigma_f \varphi - \lambda_I I, \qquad \frac{dX}{dt} = \gamma_X \Sigma_f \varphi + \lambda_I I - \lambda_X X - \sigma_X \varphi X, \qquad \rho_{\text{Xe}} = -2800\ \text{pcm} \cdot \frac{X}{X_{\text{eq}}} \]

docs.title: Fuel cycle
docs.text:
Enrichment uses the real separative work formula:

\[ V(x) = (2x - 1)\ln\frac{x}{1 - x}, \qquad \text{SWU/kg} = V(x_p) + T\,V(x_t) - F\,V(x_f), \quad x_f = 0.711\,\%,\ x_t = 0.25\,\% \] Product Natural UF₆ feed (kg/kg) SWU per kg LEU-3 5.97 3.81 LEU-4 8.13 5.83 LEU-4.5 9.22 6.87 LEU-5 10.3 7.92

Spent fuel (45 GWd/t) goes to a pool and later to PUREX reprocessing.
